idGroupoid.fullDefinition: def idGroupoid (H : Type u) [TopologicalSpace H] : StructureGroupoid H where   members := {PartialHomeomorph.refl H} ∪ { e : PartialHomeomorph H H | e.source = ∅ }   trans' e e' he he' := by     cases' he with he he     · simpa only [mem_singleton_iff.1 he, refl_trans]     · have : (e ≫ₕ e').source ⊆ e.source := sep_subset _ _       rw [he] at this       have : e ≫ₕ e' ∈ { e : PartialHomeomorph H H | e.source = ∅ } := eq_bot_iff.2 this       exact (mem_union _ _ _).2 (Or.inr this)   symm' e he := by     cases' (mem_union _ _ _).1 he with E E     · simp [mem_singleton_iff.mp E]     · right       simpa only [e.toPartialEquiv.image_source_eq_target.symm, mfld_simps] using E   id_mem' := mem_union_left _ rfl   locality' e he := by     rcases e.source.eq_empty_or_nonempty with h | h     · right       exact h     · left       rcases h with ⟨x, hx⟩       rcases he x hx with ⟨s, open_s, xs, hs⟩       have x's : x ∈ (e.restr s).source := by         rw [restr_source, open_s.interior_eq]         exact ⟨hx, xs⟩       cases' hs with hs hs       · replace hs : PartialHomeomorph.restr e s = PartialHomeomorph.refl H := by           simpa only using hs         have : (e.restr s).source = univ := by           rw [hs]           simp         have : e.toPartialEquiv.source ∩ interior s = univ := this         have : univ ⊆ interior s := by           rw [← this]           exact inter_subset_right         have : s = univ := by rwa [open_s.interior_eq, univ_subset_iff] at this         simpa only [this, restr_univ] using hs       · exfalso         rw [mem_setOf_eq] at hs         rwa [hs] at x's   mem_of_eqOnSource' e e' he he'e := by     cases' he with he he     · left       have : e = e' := by         refine eq_of_eqOnSource_univ (Setoid.symm he'e) ?_ ?_ <;>           rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff.1 he] <;> rfl       rwa [← this]     · right       have he : e.toPartialEquiv.source = ∅ := he       rwa [Set.mem_setOf_eq, EqOnSource.source_eq he'e]
idGroupoid.description: The trivial groupoid is defined as the structure groupoid that includes only the identity and maps with empty source.

Pregroupoid.property.fullDefinition: property : (H → H) → Set H → Prop   /-- The pregroupoid property is stable under composition -/   comp : ∀ {f g u v}, property f u → property g v →     IsOpen u → IsOpen v → IsOpen (u ∩ f ⁻¹' v) → property (g ∘ f) (u ∩ f ⁻¹' v)   /-- Pregroupoids contain the identity map (on `univ`) -/   id_mem : property id univ   /-- The pregroupoid property is "local", in the sense that `f` has the pregroupoid property on `u`   iff its restriction to each open subset of `u` has it -/   locality :     ∀ {f u}, IsOpen u → (∀ x ∈ u, ∃ v, IsOpen v ∧ x ∈ v ∧ property f (u ∩ v)) → property f u   /-- If `f = g` on `u` and `property f u`, then `property g u` -/   congr : ∀ {f g : H → H} {u}, IsOpen u → (∀ x ∈ u, g x = f x) → property f u → property g u
Pregroupoid.property.description: This definition describes a property that characterizes the membership of functions in a pregroupoid based on their behavior over specific subsets of a topological space.

pregroupoid.fullDefinition: property : (H → H) → Set H → Prop   /-- The pregroupoid property is stable under composition -/   comp : ∀ {f g u v}, property f u → property g v →     IsOpen u → IsOpen v → IsOpen (u ∩ f ⁻¹' v) → property (g ∘ f) (u ∩ f ⁻¹' v)   /-- Pregroupoids contain the identity map (on `univ`) -/   id_mem : property id univ   /-- The pregroupoid property is "local", in the sense that `f` has the pregroupoid property on `u`   iff its restriction to each open subset of `u` has it -/   locality :     ∀ {f u}, IsOpen u → (∀ x ∈ u, ∃ v, IsOpen v ∧ x ∈ v ∧ property f (u ∩ v)) → property f u   /-- If `f = g` on `u` and `property f u`, then `property g u` -/   congr : ∀ {f g : H → H} {u}, IsOpen u → (∀ x ∈ u, g x = f x) → property f u → property g u

Pregroupoid.groupoid.fullDefinition: def Pregroupoid.groupoid (PG : Pregroupoid H) : StructureGroupoid H where   members := { e : PartialHomeomorph H H | PG.property e e.source ∧ PG.property e.symm e.target }   trans' e e' he he' := by     constructor     · apply PG.comp he.1 he'.1 e.open_source e'.open_source       apply e.continuousOn_toFun.isOpen_inter_preimage e.open_source e'.open_source     · apply PG.comp he'.2 he.2 e'.open_target e.open_target       apply e'.continuousOn_invFun.isOpen_inter_preimage e'.open_target e.open_target   symm' e he := ⟨he.2, he.1⟩   id_mem' := ⟨PG.id_mem, PG.id_mem⟩   locality' e he := by     constructor     · refine PG.locality e.open_source fun x xu ↦ ?_       rcases he x xu with ⟨s, s_open, xs, hs⟩       refine ⟨s, s_open, xs, ?_⟩       convert hs.1 using 1       dsimp [PartialHomeomorph.restr]       rw [s_open.interior_eq]     · refine PG.locality e.open_target fun x xu ↦ ?_       rcases he (e.symm x) (e.map_target xu) with ⟨s, s_open, xs, hs⟩       refine ⟨e.target ∩ e.symm ⁻¹' s, ?_, ⟨xu, xs⟩, ?_⟩       · exact ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage e.continuousOn_invFun e.open_target s_open       · rw [← inter_assoc, inter_self]         convert hs.2 using 1         dsimp [PartialHomeomorph.restr]         rw [s_open.interior_eq]   mem_of_eqOnSource' e e' he ee' := by     constructor     · apply PG.congr e'.open_source ee'.2       simp only [ee'.1, he.1]     · have A := EqOnSource.symm' ee'       apply PG.congr e'.symm.open_source A.2       -- Porting note: was       -- convert he.2       -- rw [A.1]       -- rfl       rw [A.1, symm_toPartialEquiv, PartialEquiv.symm_source]       exact he.2
Pregroupoid.groupoid.description: A groupoid of partial homeomorphisms is constructed from a pregroupoid, ensuring that the properties of the maps and their inverses are preserved under composition.

idRestrGroupoid.fullDefinition: def idRestrGroupoid : StructureGroupoid H where   members := { e | ∃ (s : Set H) (h : IsOpen s), e ≈ PartialHomeomorph.ofSet s h }   trans' := by     rintro e e' ⟨s, hs, hse⟩ ⟨s', hs', hse'⟩     refine ⟨s ∩ s', hs.inter hs', ?_⟩     have := PartialHomeomorph.EqOnSource.trans' hse hse'     rwa [PartialHomeomorph.ofSet_trans_ofSet] at this   symm' := by     rintro e ⟨s, hs, hse⟩     refine ⟨s, hs, ?_⟩     rw [← ofSet_symm]     exact PartialHomeomorph.EqOnSource.symm' hse   id_mem' := ⟨univ, isOpen_univ, by simp only [mfld_simps, refl]⟩   locality' := by     intro e h     refine ⟨e.source, e.open_source, by simp only [mfld_simps], ?_⟩     intro x hx     rcases h x hx with ⟨s, hs, hxs, s', hs', hes'⟩     have hes : x ∈ (e.restr s).source := by       rw [e.restr_source]       refine ⟨hx, ?_⟩       rw [hs.interior_eq]       exact hxs     simpa only [mfld_simps] using PartialHomeomorph.EqOnSource.eqOn hes' hes   mem_of_eqOnSource' := by     rintro e e' ⟨s, hs, hse⟩ hee'     exact ⟨s, hs, Setoid.trans hee' hse⟩

ChartedSpaceCore.partialHomeomorph.fullDefinition: protected def partialHomeomorph (e : PartialEquiv M H) (he : e ∈ c.atlas) :     @PartialHomeomorph M H c.toTopologicalSpace _ :=   { __ := c.toTopologicalSpace     __ := e     open_source := by convert c.open_source' he     open_target := by convert c.open_target he     continuousOn_toFun := by       letI : TopologicalSpace M := c.toTopologicalSpace       rw [continuousOn_open_iff (c.open_source' he)]       intro s s_open       rw [inter_comm]       apply TopologicalSpace.GenerateOpen.basic       simp only [exists_prop, mem_iUnion, mem_singleton_iff]       exact ⟨e, he, ⟨s, s_open, rfl⟩⟩     continuousOn_invFun := by       letI : TopologicalSpace M := c.toTopologicalSpace       apply continuousOn_isOpen_of_generateFrom       intro t ht       simp only [exists_prop, mem_iUnion, mem_singleton_iff] at ht       rcases ht with ⟨e', e'_atlas, s, s_open, ts⟩       rw [ts]       let f := e.symm.trans e'       have : IsOpen (f ⁻¹' s ∩ f.source) := by         simpa [f, inter_comm] using (continuousOn_open_iff (c.open_source e e' he e'_atlas)).1           (c.continuousOn_toFun e e' he e'_atlas) s s_open       have A : e' ∘ e.symm ⁻¹' s ∩ (e.target ∩ e.symm ⁻¹' e'.source) =           e.target ∩ (e' ∘ e.symm ⁻¹' s ∩ e.symm ⁻¹' e'.source) := by         rw [← inter_assoc, ← inter_assoc]         congr 1         exact inter_comm _ _       simpa [f, PartialEquiv.trans_source, preimage_inter, preimage_comp.symm, A] using this }

explanatories.ChartedSpaceCore.open_source: This theorem indicates that if two partial equivalences of a charted space are members of its atlas, then the source of their composition is an open set.
explanatories.Set.preimage_inter: The preimage of the intersection of two sets under a function is equal to the intersection of the preimages of those sets under the same function.

explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.

PartialHomeomorph.singletonChartedSpace.comment:
If a single partial homeomorphism `e` from a space `α` into `H` has source covering the whole
space `α`, then that partial homeomorphism induces an `H`-charted space structure on `α`.
(This condition is equivalent to `e` being an open embedding of `α` into `H`; see
`OpenEmbedding.singletonChartedSpace`.)

explanatories.StructureGroupoid.symm: The theorem states that the inverse of a partial homeomorphism is also a member of the structure groupoid if the original homeomorphism is a member.
explanatories.StructureGroupoid.mem_of_eqOnSource: This theorem establishes that if a partial homeomorphism is a member of a structure groupoid and another partial homeomorphism is equivalent to it, then the latter is also a member of the groupoid.
explanatories.Setoid.symm: The symmetry property of an equivalence relation asserts that if one element is equivalent to another, then the second element is also equivalent to the first.
explanatories.Set.mem_singleton_iff: An element belongs to a singleton set if and only if it is equal to the unique element in that set.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Set.EqOn.symm: The theorem asserts that if two functions are equal on a specified set, then they are also equal on that set when the order of the functions is reversed.
explanatories.closedUnderRestriction': If a partial homeomorphism belongs to a structure groupoid and is restricted to an open subset, then the restriction remains a member of the groupoid.
explanatories.chart_mem_atlas: This theorem asserts that the chart associated with a point in a topological space belongs to the atlas defined for that space.
explanatories.PartialEquiv.symm: This defines the inverse of a partial equivalence, allowing for a corresponding mapping from one type back to another.
explanatories.ChartedSpaceCore.chart_mem_atlas: The chart at a point in a charted space is an element of the atlas associated with that space.
explanatories.HasGroupoid.compatible: This theorem asserts that if two partial homeomorphisms belong to the atlas of a charted space, then the composition of the first one's inverse with the second is also a member of the associated structure groupoid.
explanatories.StructureGroupoid.compatible: This theorem reformulates the compatibility condition for charts in a charted space with an associated structure groupoid, asserting that the composition of the inverse of one partial homeomorphism with another is also a member of that structure groupoid.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.isOpen_inter_preimage_: This theorem asserts that the intersection of the target set of a partial homeomorphism with the pre-image of an open set is itself open.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.subtypeRestr_symm_tran: This theorem describes how the composition of two restricted partial homeomorphisms can be related to the transition of the original functions when applied to an open subset, utilizing their inverses and intersections with the target sets.
explanatories.Homeomorph.symm: This definition establishes the inverse of a homeomorphism, mapping a homeomorphism from one topological space to its corresponding homeomorphism in the reverse direction.

TopologicalSpace.Opens.instHasGroupoid.fullDefinition: protected instance instHasGroupoid [ClosedUnderRestriction G] : HasGroupoid s G where   compatible := by     rintro e e' ⟨_, ⟨x, hc⟩, he⟩ ⟨_, ⟨x', hc'⟩, he'⟩     rw [hc.symm, mem_singleton_iff] at he     rw [hc'.symm, mem_singleton_iff] at he'     rw [he, he']     refine G.mem_of_eqOnSource ?_       (subtypeRestr_symm_trans_subtypeRestr (s := s) _ (chartAt H x) (chartAt H x'))     apply closedUnderRestriction'     · exact G.compatible (chart_mem_atlas _ _) (chart_mem_atlas _ _)     · exact isOpen_inter_preimage_symm (chartAt _ _) s.2
TopologicalSpace.Opens.instHasGroupoid.description: This definition establishes that if a groupoid is closed under restriction, then any open subset of a space that possesses a groupoid structure with respect to this groupoid also retains that structure.

Structomorph.refl.fullDefinition: def Structomorph.refl (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [HasGroupoid M G] :     Structomorph G M M :=   { Homeomorph.refl M with     mem_groupoid := fun c c' hc hc' ↦ by       change PartialHomeomorph.symm c ≫ₕ PartialHomeomorph.refl M ≫ₕ c' ∈ G       rw [PartialHomeomorph.refl_trans]       exact G.compatible hc hc' }

structomorph.refl.fullDefinition: def Structomorph.refl (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [HasGroupoid M G] :     Structomorph G M M :=   { Homeomorph.refl M with     mem_groupoid := fun c c' hc hc' ↦ by       change PartialHomeomorph.symm c ≫ₕ PartialHomeomorph.refl M ≫ₕ c' ∈ G       rw [PartialHomeomorph.refl_trans]       exact G.compatible hc hc' }

Structomorph.trans.fullDefinition: def Structomorph.trans (e : Structomorph G M M') (e' : Structomorph G M' M'') :     Structomorph G M M'' :=   { Homeomorph.trans e.toHomeomorph e'.toHomeomorph with     mem_groupoid := by       /- Let c and c' be two charts in M and M''. We want to show that e' ∘ e is smooth in these       charts, around any point x. For this, let y = e (c⁻¹ x), and consider a chart g around y.       Then g ∘ e ∘ c⁻¹ and c' ∘ e' ∘ g⁻¹ are both smooth as e and e' are structomorphisms, so       their composition is smooth, and it coincides with c' ∘ e' ∘ e ∘ c⁻¹ around x. -/       intro c c' hc hc'       refine G.locality fun x hx ↦ ?_       let f₁ := e.toHomeomorph.toPartialHomeomorph       let f₂ := e'.toHomeomorph.toPartialHomeomorph       let f := (e.toHomeomorph.trans e'.toHomeomorph).toPartialHomeomorph       have feq : f = f₁ ≫ₕ f₂ := Homeomorph.trans_toPartialHomeomorph _ _       -- define the atlas g around y       let y := (c.symm ≫ₕ f₁) x       let g := chartAt (H := H) y       have hg₁ := chart_mem_atlas (H := H) y       have hg₂ := mem_chart_source (H := H) y       let s := (c.symm ≫ₕ f₁).source ∩ c.symm ≫ₕ f₁ ⁻¹' g.source       have open_s : IsOpen s := by         apply (c.symm ≫ₕ f₁).continuousOn_toFun.isOpen_inter_preimage <;> apply open_source       have : x ∈ s := by         constructor         · simp only [f₁, trans_source, preimage_univ, inter_univ,             Homeomorph.toPartialHomeomorph_source]           rw [trans_source] at hx           exact hx.1         · exact hg₂       refine ⟨s, open_s, this, ?_⟩       let F₁ := (c.symm ≫ₕ f₁ ≫ₕ g) ≫ₕ g.symm ≫ₕ f₂ ≫ₕ c'       have A : F₁ ∈ G := G.trans (e.mem_groupoid c g hc hg₁) (e'.mem_groupoid g c' hg₁ hc')       let F₂ := (c.symm ≫ₕ f ≫ₕ c').restr s       have : F₁ ≈ F₂ := calc         F₁ ≈ c.symm ≫ₕ f₁ ≫ₕ (g ≫ₕ g.symm) ≫ₕ f₂ ≫ₕ c' := by             simp only [F₁, trans_assoc, _root_.refl]         _ ≈ c.symm ≫ₕ f₁ ≫ₕ ofSet g.source g.open_source ≫ₕ f₂ ≫ₕ c' :=           EqOnSource.trans' (_root_.refl _) (EqOnSource.trans' (_root_.refl _)             (EqOnSource.trans' (self_trans_symm g) (_root_.refl _)))         _ ≈ ((c.symm ≫ₕ f₁) ≫ₕ ofSet g.source g.open_source) ≫ₕ f₂ ≫ₕ c' := by           simp only [trans_assoc, _root_.refl]         _ ≈ (c.symm ≫ₕ f₁).restr s ≫ₕ f₂ ≫ₕ c' := by rw [trans_of_set']         _ ≈ ((c.symm ≫ₕ f₁) ≫ₕ f₂ ≫ₕ c').restr s := by rw [restr_trans]         _ ≈ (c.symm ≫ₕ (f₁ ≫ₕ f₂) ≫ₕ c').restr s := by           simp only [EqOnSource.restr, trans_assoc, _root_.refl]         _ ≈ F₂ := by simp only [F₂, feq, _root_.refl]       have : F₂ ∈ G := G.mem_of_eqOnSource A (Setoid.symm this)       exact this }

explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.open_source: This theorem states that the source of a partial homeomorphism is an open set in the associated topological space.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.continuousOn_toFun: This theorem establishes that the function derived from a partial homeomorphism is continuous on its defined source set.
explanatories.ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage: The intersection of an open set with the preimage of another open set under a continuous function is open.
explanatories.Pregroupoid.locality: The theorem states that a function possesses the pregroupoid property on a set if it does so locally on each open subset within that set.
explanatories.Set.EqOn.symm: The theorem asserts that if two functions are equal on a specified set, then they are also equal on that set when the order of the functions is reversed.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.ofSet: This definition describes a partial homeomorphism that is associated with an open set within a topological space, effectively acting as an identity mapping on that set.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.EqOnSource.trans': This theorem states that if two partial homeomorphisms are equivalent, then their compositions with another partial homeomorphism also remain equivalent.
explanatories.refl: This theorem states that if a binary relation is reflexive, then any element is related to itself under that relation.
explanatories.Setoid.trans: If two elements are related by a relation and the second element is related to a third element, then the first and third elements are also related by the same relation.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.EqOnSource.restr: This theorem states that if two partial homeomorphisms are equivalent, their restrictions to a common subset are also equivalent.
explanatories.chartAt: This definition specifies the preferred chart at a given point in a charted space, representing a partial homeomorphism between the manifold and the Euclidean space.
explanatories.atlas: The atlas of charts in a charted space represents a set of partial homeomorphisms that relate two topological spaces.
explanatories.mem_chart_source: This theorem asserts that a point belonging to a charted space is included in the source set of the chart at that point.
explanatories.chart_mem_atlas: This theorem asserts that the chart associated with a point in a topological space belongs to the atlas defined for that space.
explanatories.ChartedSpace.atlas: The atlas of charts in a charted space comprises a set of partial homeomorphisms between the manifold and the topological space.
explanatories.PartialEquiv.symm: This defines the inverse of a partial equivalence, allowing for a corresponding mapping from one type back to another.
explanatories.ChartedSpaceCore.atlas: This definition describes an atlas of charts for a charted space as a set of partial equivalences between two types.
explanatories.Set.preimage_univ: The preimage of the universal set under any function is the universal set itself.
explanatories.PartialEquiv.trans_source: This theorem states that the source of the composition of two partial equivalences is equal to the intersection of the original source and the preimage of the source of the second equivalence under the first.
explanatories.ChartedSpaceCore.open_source: This theorem indicates that if two partial equivalences of a charted space are members of its atlas, then the source of their composition is an open set.
explanatories.ChartedSpaceCore.chartAt: This definition specifies a function that assigns a particular partial equivalence between a manifold and its corresponding space at each point of the manifold.
explanatories.ChartedSpaceCore.chart_mem_atlas: The chart at a point in a charted space is an element of the atlas associated with that space.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.trans_assoc: This theorem states that the composition of partial homeomorphisms is associative.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.self_trans_symm: This theorem states that the composition of a partial homeomorphism with its inverse is equivalent to the identity mapping restricted to the source of the homeomorphism.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.trans_of_set': This theorem establishes that the composition of a partial homeomorphism with a restriction to a set can be expressed as the restriction of the original homeomorphism to the intersection of its source with the preimage of an open set.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.restr_trans: This theorem shows that the restriction of the composition of two partial homeomorphisms is equivalent to the composition of their restrictions to a specified set.
explanatories.OpenEmbedding.toPartialHomeomorph: An open embedding from one topological space to another, given that the first space is nonempty, provides a way to define a partial homeomorphism that encompasses the entire structure of the first space.
explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.
explanatories.Homeomorph.toPartialHomeomorph: This definition describes how a homeomorphism translates into a partial homeomorphism that applies to the entire space.
explanatories.Homeomorph.refl: This defines the identity map as a homeomorphism for a given topological space.
explanatories.Structomorph.refl: The definition establishes that the identity map is a diffeomorphism for any charted space within the context of a given structure groupoid.
explanatories.Structomorph.toHomeomorph: This definition states that a structomorphism between two charted spaces induces a homeomorphism between their underlying topological spaces.
explanatories.Homeomorph.symm: This definition establishes the inverse of a homeomorphism, mapping a homeomorphism from one topological space to its corresponding homeomorphism in the reverse direction.
explanatories.Structomorph.mem_groupoid: If two partial homeomorphisms are part of the atlases of two charted spaces and the composite of their inverses and a structomorph between the corresponding structure groupoid is taken, then this composite is an element of that groupoid.
explanatories.Structomorph.symm: The inverse of a structomorphism between two topological spaces is also a structomorphism relating the same spaces in the opposite direction.
explanatories.Homeomorph.trans: This defines the composition of two homeomorphisms between topological spaces, resulting in a homeomorphism between the first and the third spaces.
explanatories.Homeomorph.trans_toPartialHomeomorph: This theorem confirms that the composition of two homeomorphisms, when converted to partial homeomorphisms, maintains the order of the transformations and is equivalent to the direct composition of their corresponding partial homeomorphisms.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.trans_source: This theorem establishes that the source set of the composition of two partial homeomorphisms is equal to the intersection of the source of the first homeomorphism and the pre-image under the first homeomorphism of the source of the second homeomorphism.
explanatories.Set.inter_univ: The intersection of any set with the universal set is equal to that set.

structomorph.trans.fullDefinition: def Structomorph.trans (e : Structomorph G M M') (e' : Structomorph G M' M'') :     Structomorph G M M'' :=   { Homeomorph.trans e.toHomeomorph e'.toHomeomorph with     mem_groupoid := by       /- Let c and c' be two charts in M and M''. We want to show that e' ∘ e is smooth in these       charts, around any point x. For this, let y = e (c⁻¹ x), and consider a chart g around y.       Then g ∘ e ∘ c⁻¹ and c' ∘ e' ∘ g⁻¹ are both smooth as e and e' are structomorphisms, so       their composition is smooth, and it coincides with c' ∘ e' ∘ e ∘ c⁻¹ around x. -/       intro c c' hc hc'       refine G.locality fun x hx ↦ ?_       let f₁ := e.toHomeomorph.toPartialHomeomorph       let f₂ := e'.toHomeomorph.toPartialHomeomorph       let f := (e.toHomeomorph.trans e'.toHomeomorph).toPartialHomeomorph       have feq : f = f₁ ≫ₕ f₂ := Homeomorph.trans_toPartialHomeomorph _ _       -- define the atlas g around y       let y := (c.symm ≫ₕ f₁) x       let g := chartAt (H := H) y       have hg₁ := chart_mem_atlas (H := H) y       have hg₂ := mem_chart_source (H := H) y       let s := (c.symm ≫ₕ f₁).source ∩ c.symm ≫ₕ f₁ ⁻¹' g.source       have open_s : IsOpen s := by         apply (c.symm ≫ₕ f₁).continuousOn_toFun.isOpen_inter_preimage <;> apply open_source       have : x ∈ s := by         constructor         · simp only [f₁, trans_source, preimage_univ, inter_univ,             Homeomorph.toPartialHomeomorph_source]           rw [trans_source] at hx           exact hx.1         · exact hg₂       refine ⟨s, open_s, this, ?_⟩       let F₁ := (c.symm ≫ₕ f₁ ≫ₕ g) ≫ₕ g.symm ≫ₕ f₂ ≫ₕ c'       have A : F₁ ∈ G := G.trans (e.mem_groupoid c g hc hg₁) (e'.mem_groupoid g c' hg₁ hc')       let F₂ := (c.symm ≫ₕ f ≫ₕ c').restr s       have : F₁ ≈ F₂ := calc         F₁ ≈ c.symm ≫ₕ f₁ ≫ₕ (g ≫ₕ g.symm) ≫ₕ f₂ ≫ₕ c' := by             simp only [F₁, trans_assoc, _root_.refl]         _ ≈ c.symm ≫ₕ f₁ ≫ₕ ofSet g.source g.open_source ≫ₕ f₂ ≫ₕ c' :=           EqOnSource.trans' (_root_.refl _) (EqOnSource.trans' (_root_.refl _)             (EqOnSource.trans' (self_trans_symm g) (_root_.refl _)))         _ ≈ ((c.symm ≫ₕ f₁) ≫ₕ ofSet g.source g.open_source) ≫ₕ f₂ ≫ₕ c' := by           simp only [trans_assoc, _root_.refl]         _ ≈ (c.symm ≫ₕ f₁).restr s ≫ₕ f₂ ≫ₕ c' := by rw [trans_of_set']         _ ≈ ((c.symm ≫ₕ f₁) ≫ₕ f₂ ≫ₕ c').restr s := by rw [restr_trans]         _ ≈ (c.symm ≫ₕ (f₁ ≫ₕ f₂) ≫ₕ c').restr s := by           simp only [EqOnSource.restr, trans_assoc, _root_.refl]         _ ≈ F₂ := by simp only [F₂, feq, _root_.refl]       have : F₂ ∈ G := G.mem_of_eqOnSource A (Setoid.symm this)       exact this }
structomorph.trans.description: This definition asserts that the composition of two structomorphisms between topological spaces results in another structomorphism within the same structure groupoid.

StructureGroupoid.mem_maximalAtlas_of_eq.comment: The maximal atlas of a structure groupoid is stable under equivalence.

explanatories.ChartedSpace: The atlas of charts in a charted space comprises a set of partial homeomorphisms between the manifold and the topological space.
explanatories.StructureGroupoid.maximalAtlas: This definition characterizes the maximal atlas for a structure groupoid on a charted space as the collection of all charts that maintain compatibility with the existing atlas by ensuring that changes in coordinates yield elements of the groupoid.

StructureGroupoid.mem_maximalAtlas_of_eq.description: The theorem asserts that if two partial homeomorphisms are equivalent and one belongs to the maximal atlas of a structure groupoid, then the other also belongs to that maximal atlas.

StructureGroupoid.restriction_in_maximal.code:
StructureGroupoid.restriction_in_maximalAtlas.{u, u_2} {H : Type u} {M : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace H]
  [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] {e : PartialHomeomorph M H} (he : e ∈ atlas H M) {s : Opens M}
  (hs : Nonempty ↥s) {G : StructureGroupoid H} [HasGroupoid M G] [ClosedUnderRestriction G] :
  e.subtypeRestr hs ∈ maximalAtlas (↥s) G
StructureGroupoid.restriction_in_maximal.comment:
Restricting a chart of `M` to an open subset `s` yields a chart in the maximal atlas of `s`.

NB. We cannot deduce membership in `atlas H s` in general: by definition, this atlas contains
precisely the restriction of each preferred chart at `x ∈ s` --- whereas `atlas H M`
can contain more charts than these.

StructureGroupoid.LocalInvariantProp.liftPropWithinAt_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {H : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2}

  {P : (H → H') → Set H → H → Prop} {s : Set M} {x : M} (hG : G.LocalInvariantProp G' P) {f : M → M'} :
  LiftPropWithinAt P f s x ↔
    ContinuousWithinAt f s x ∧
      P (↑(chartAt H' (f x)) ∘ f ∘ ↑(chartAt H x).symm)
        ((chartAt H x).target ∩ ↑(chartAt H x).symm ⁻¹' (s ∩ f ⁻¹' (chartAt H' (f x)).source)) (↑(chartAt H x) x)
StructureGroupoid.LocalInvariantProp.lif.comment:
`LiftPropWithinAt P f s x` is equivalent to a definition where we restrict the set we are
considering to the domain of the charts at `x` and `f x`.

StructureGroupoid.LocalInvariantProp.lif.comment:
If a property of a germ of function `g` on a pointed set `(s, x)` is invariant under the
structure groupoid (by composition in the source space and in the target space), then
expressing it in charted spaces does not depend on the element of the maximal atlas one uses
both in the source and in the target manifolds, provided they are defined around `x` and `g x`
respectively, and provided `g` is continuous within `s` at `x` (otherwise, the local behavior
of `g` at `x` can not be captured with a chart in the target).

StructureGroupoid.IsLocalStructomorphWit.comment:
A function from a model space `H` to itself is a local structomorphism, with respect to a
structure groupoid `G` for `H`, relative to a set `s` in `H`, if for all points `x` in the set, the
function agrees with a `G`-structomorphism on `s` in a neighbourhood of `x`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.PartialEquiv.source: This defines the domain of a partial equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Set.EqOn: Two functions are considered equal on a specified set if they produce the same output for every input from that set.
explanatories.PartialEquiv.toFun: This function provides a partial mapping from one type to another, where its output is only meaningful within a specified subset of the first type.

StructureGroupoid.IsLocalStructomorphWit.fullDefinition: def IsLocalStructomorphWithinAt (f : H → H) (s : Set H) (x : H) : Prop :=   x ∈ s → ∃ e : PartialHomeomorph H H, e ∈ G ∧ EqOn f e.toFun (s ∩ e.source) ∧ x ∈ e.source
StructureGroupoid.IsLocalStructomorphWit.description: A function is defined as a local structomorphism relative to a structure groupoid if it behaves like a groupoid-structured morphism on a neighborhood of each point within a specified set.

StructureGroupoid.LocalInvariantProp.loc.comment:
Let `P` be a `LocalInvariantProp` for functions between spaces with the groupoids `G`, `G'`
and let `M`, `M'` be charted spaces modelled on the model spaces of those groupoids.  Then there is
an induced `LocalPredicate` on the functions from `M` to `M'`, given by `LiftProp P`.

StructureGroupoid.LocalInvariantProp.loc.fullDefinition: def StructureGroupoid.LocalInvariantProp.localPredicate (hG : LocalInvariantProp G G' P) :     TopCat.LocalPredicate fun _ : TopCat.of M => M' where   pred {U : Opens (TopCat.of M)} := fun f : U → M' => ChartedSpace.LiftProp P f   res := by     intro U V i f h x     have hUV : U ≤ V := CategoryTheory.leOfHom i     show ChartedSpace.LiftPropAt P (f ∘ Set.inclusion hUV) x     rw [← hG.liftPropAt_iff_comp_inclusion hUV]     apply h   locality := by     intro V f h x     obtain ⟨U, hxU, i, hU : ChartedSpace.LiftProp P (f ∘ i)⟩ := h x     let x' : U := ⟨x, hxU⟩     have hUV : U ≤ V := CategoryTheory.leOfHom i     have : ChartedSpace.LiftPropAt P f (inclusion hUV x') := by       rw [hG.liftPropAt_iff_comp_inclusion hUV]       exact hU x'     convert this

ModelWithCorners.prod.comment:
Given two model_with_corners `I` on `(E, H)` and `I'` on `(E', H')`, we define the model with
corners `I.prod I'` on `(E × E', ModelProd H H')`. This appears in particular for the manifold
structure on the tangent bundle to a manifold modelled on `(E, H)`: it will be modelled on
`(E × E, H × E)`. See note [Manifold type tags] for explanation about `ModelProd H H'`
vs `H × H'`.

ModelWithCorners.prod.fullDefinition: def ModelWithCorners.prod {𝕜 : Type u} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type v}     [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type w} [TopologicalSpace H]     (I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H) {E' : Type v'} [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E']     {H' : Type w'} [TopologicalSpace H'] (I' : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E' H') :     ModelWithCorners 𝕜 (E × E') (ModelProd H H') :=   { I.toPartialEquiv.prod I'.toPartialEquiv with     toFun := fun x => (I x.1, I' x.2)     invFun := fun x => (I.symm x.1, I'.symm x.2)     source := { x | x.1 ∈ I.source ∧ x.2 ∈ I'.source }     source_eq := by simp only [setOf_true, mfld_simps]     unique_diff' := I.unique_diff'.prod I'.unique_diff'     continuous_toFun := I.continuous_toFun.prod_map I'.continuous_toFun     continuous_invFun := I.continuous_invFun.prod_map I'.continuous_invFun }

ModelWithCorners.pi.fullDefinition: def ModelWithCorners.pi {𝕜 : Type u} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {ι : Type v} [Fintype ι]     {E : ι → Type w} [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (E i)] [∀ i, NormedSpace 𝕜 (E i)] {H : ι → Type u'}     [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (H i)] (I : ∀ i, ModelWithCorners 𝕜 (E i) (H i)) :     ModelWithCorners 𝕜 (∀ i, E i) (ModelPi H) where   toPartialEquiv := PartialEquiv.pi fun i => (I i).toPartialEquiv   source_eq := by simp only [pi_univ, mfld_simps]   unique_diff' := UniqueDiffOn.pi ι E _ _ fun i _ => (I i).unique_diff'   continuous_toFun := continuous_pi fun i => (I i).continuous.comp (continuous_apply i)   continuous_invFun := continuous_pi fun i => (I i).continuous_symm.comp (continuous_apply i)

contDiffPregroupoid.fullDefinition: def contDiffPregroupoid : Pregroupoid H where   property f s := ContDiffOn 𝕜 n (I ∘ f ∘ I.symm) (I.symm ⁻¹' s ∩ range I)   comp {f g u v} hf hg _ _ _ := by     have : I ∘ (g ∘ f) ∘ I.symm = (I ∘ g ∘ I.symm) ∘ I ∘ f ∘ I.symm := by ext x; simp     simp only [this]     refine hg.comp (hf.mono fun x ⟨hx1, hx2⟩ ↦ ⟨hx1.1, hx2⟩) ?_     rintro x ⟨hx1, _⟩     simp only [mfld_simps] at hx1 ⊢     exact hx1.2   id_mem := by     apply ContDiffOn.congr contDiff_id.contDiffOn     rintro x ⟨_, hx2⟩     rcases mem_range.1 hx2 with ⟨y, hy⟩     rw [← hy]     simp only [mfld_simps]   locality {f u} _ H := by     apply contDiffOn_of_locally_contDiffOn     rintro y ⟨hy1, hy2⟩     rcases mem_range.1 hy2 with ⟨x, hx⟩     rw [← hx] at hy1 ⊢     simp only [mfld_simps] at hy1 ⊢     rcases H x hy1 with ⟨v, v_open, xv, hv⟩     have : I.symm ⁻¹' (u ∩ v) ∩ range I = I.symm ⁻¹' u ∩ range I ∩ I.symm ⁻¹' v := by       rw [preimage_inter, inter_assoc, inter_assoc]       congr 1       rw [inter_comm]     rw [this] at hv     exact ⟨I.symm ⁻¹' v, v_open.preimage I.continuous_symm, by simpa, hv⟩   congr {f g u} _ fg hf := by     apply hf.congr     rintro y ⟨hy1, hy2⟩     rcases mem_range.1 hy2 with ⟨x, hx⟩     rw [← hx] at hy1 ⊢     simp only [mfld_simps] at hy1 ⊢     rw [fg _ hy1]

explanatories.contDiffGroupoid_prod: This theorem states that the product of two smooth partial homeomorphisms is also smooth within the context of their respective models with corners.
explanatories.StructureGroupoid.compatible: This theorem reformulates the compatibility condition for charts in a charted space with an associated structure groupoid, asserting that the composition of the inverse of one partial homeomorphism with another is also a member of that structure groupoid.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.prod_symm: This theorem states that the inverse of the product of two partial homeomorphisms is equal to the product of their respective inverses.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.prod_trans: This theorem asserts that the composition of two pairs of partial homeomorphisms, one from each pair, commutes with the product of those pairs.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.

SmoothManifoldWithCorners.prod.fullDefinition: instance prod {𝕜 : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]     [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {E' : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E'] {H : Type*}     [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H} {H' : Type*} [TopologicalSpace H']     {I' : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E' H'} (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]     [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M] (M' : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M'] [ChartedSpace H' M']     [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I' M'] : SmoothManifoldWithCorners (I.prod I') (M × M') where   compatible := by     rintro f g ⟨f1, hf1, f2, hf2, rfl⟩ ⟨g1, hg1, g2, hg2, rfl⟩     rw [PartialHomeomorph.prod_symm, PartialHomeomorph.prod_trans]     have h1 := (contDiffGroupoid ⊤ I).compatible hf1 hg1     have h2 := (contDiffGroupoid ⊤ I').compatible hf2 hg2     exact contDiffGroupoid_prod h1 h2

  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H}
  {M : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] {E' : Type u_5} [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E']
  {H' : Type u_6} [TopologicalSpace H'] {I' : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E' H'} {M' : Type u_7} [TopologicalSpace M']
  [ChartedSpace H' M'] {f : M → M'} {s : Set M} {x : M} {n : ℕ∞} :
  ContMDiffWithinAt I I' n f s x ↔
    ContinuousWithinAt f s x ∧
      ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 n (↑(extChartAt I' (f x)) ∘ f ∘ ↑(extChartAt I x).symm)
        (↑(extChartAt I x).symm ⁻¹' s ∩ range ↑I) (↑(extChartAt I x) x)

contMDiffOn_iff_of_subset_source'.code:
contMDiffOn_iff_of_subset_source'.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
  {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace H]
  {I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H} {M : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M]
  {E' : Type u_5} [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E'] {H' : Type u_6} [TopologicalSpace H']
  {I' : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E' H'} {M' : Type u_7} [TopologicalSpace M'] [ChartedSpace H' M']
  [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I' M'] {f : M → M'} {s : Set M} {n : ℕ∞} {x : M} {y : M'}
  (hs : s ⊆ (extChartAt I x).source) (h2s : MapsTo f s (extChartAt I' y).source) :
  ContMDiffOn I I' n f s ↔ ContDiffOn 𝕜 n (↑(extChartAt I' y) ∘ f ∘ ↑(extChartAt I x).symm) (↑(extChartAt I x) '' s)
contMDiffOn_iff_of_subset_source'.comment:
If the set where you want `f` to be smooth lies entirely in a single chart, and `f` maps it
into a single chart, the smoothness of `f` on that set can be expressed by purely looking in
these charts.
Note: this lemma uses `extChartAt I x '' s` instead of `(extChartAt I x).symm ⁻¹' s` to ensure
that this set lies in `(extChartAt I x).target`.

  LiftPropOn (contDiffGroupoid ⊤ I).IsLocalStructomorphWithinAt (↑f) f.source ↔
    SmoothOn I I (↑f) f.source ∧ SmoothOn I I (↑f.symm) f.target
isLocalStructomorphOn_contDiffGroupoid_i.comment:
Let `M` and `M'` be smooth manifolds with the same model-with-corners, `I`.  Then `f : M → M'`
is a local structomorphism for `I`, if and only if it is manifold-smooth on the domain of definition
in both directions.

Smooth.smul.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_18} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H} {M : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace H M] {V : Type u_18} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V] {f : M → 𝕜} {g : M → V}
  (hf : Smooth I 𝓘(𝕜, 𝕜) f) (hg : Smooth I 𝓘(𝕜, V) g) : Smooth I 𝓘(𝕜, V) fun p => f p • g p

explanatories.ContMDiffWithinAt.smul: This theorem asserts that if two functions are continuously differentiable at a point within a manifold, one being a function that maps to a field and the other mapping to a normed vector space, then their pointwise scalar multiplication is also continuously differentiable at that point.
explanatories.ContMDiffAt.smul: This theorem establishes that if two functions are continuously differentiable at a point, one with respect to real numbers and the other with respect to a vector space, their product (via scalar multiplication) is also continuously differentiable at that point.
explanatories.ContMDiffOn.smul: This theorem states that the product of a continuously differentiable scalar function and a continuously differentiable vector function is also continuously differentiable on a specified set.
explanatories.ContMDiff.smul: This theorem states that if two functions are continuously differentiable on a manifold, then their pointwise product, where one function is a scalar field and the other is a vector field, is also continuously differentiable on that manifold.
explanatories.SmoothWithinAt.smul: This theorem states that if two functions are smooth at a point within a set, one mapping from a manifold to a scalar and the other to a vector space, then their pointwise scalar multiplication is also smooth at that point within the same set.
explanatories.SmoothAt.smul: This theorem asserts that if two functions are smooth at a point on a manifold, with one mapping to a field and the other to a vector space, then their product formed by taking a scalar multiplication is also smooth at that point.
explanatories.SmoothOn.smul: This theorem shows that if two functions are smooth on a set, then their pointwise scalar multiplication is also smooth on that set.

modelWithCornersEuclideanHalfSpace.fullDefinition: def modelWithCornersEuclideanHalfSpace (n : ℕ) [Zero (Fin n)] :     ModelWithCorners ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (EuclideanHalfSpace n) where   toFun := Subtype.val   invFun x := ⟨update x 0 (max (x 0) 0), by simp [le_refl]⟩   source := univ   target := { x | 0 ≤ x 0 }   map_source' x _ := x.property   map_target' _ _ := mem_univ _   left_inv' := fun ⟨xval, xprop⟩ _ => by     rw [Subtype.mk_eq_mk, update_eq_iff]     exact ⟨max_eq_left xprop, fun i _ => rfl⟩   right_inv' x hx := update_eq_iff.2 ⟨max_eq_left hx, fun i _ => rfl⟩   source_eq := rfl   unique_diff' := by     have : UniqueDiffOn ℝ _ :=       UniqueDiffOn.pi (Fin n) (fun _ => ℝ) _ _ fun i (_ : i ∈ ({0} : Set (Fin n))) =>         uniqueDiffOn_Ici 0     simpa only [singleton_pi] using this   continuous_toFun := continuous_subtype_val   continuous_invFun := by     exact (continuous_id.update 0 <| (continuous_apply 0).max continuous_const).subtype_mk _

explanatories.Subtype.property: This theorem states that for any element of a subtype defined by a property, that element satisfies the property itself.
explanatories.Subtype.mk_eq_mk: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if and only if their corresponding underlying elements are equal, given that both satisfy the same property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.continuous_subtype_val: This theorem states that the value function of a subtype in a topological space is continuous.
explanatories.continuous_id: The identity function is continuous in any topological space.
explanatories.continuous_apply: This theorem states that if each type in a family of types has a topology, then the function that selects the component of a dependent pair based on its index is continuous.
explanatories.continuous_const: The constant function from one topological space to another is continuous.
explanatories.Continuous.subtype_mk: This theorem establishes that if a function is continuous and maps into a subset defined by a property, then the function extended to create a subtype from its output remains continuous.
explanatories.continuous_pi: This theorem establishes that if a family of functions from a topological space to another type is continuous for each index, then the overall function defined by these family members is also continuous.
explanatories.Continuous.comp: The composition of two continuous functions in topological spaces is itself continuous.
explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.
explanatories.sub_nonneg: This theorem states that a non-negative difference between two elements is equivalent to one element being less than or equal to the other in an additive group.
explanatories.And.left: From a conjunction of two propositions, it is possible to extract and prove the first proposition.
explanatories.Min.min: This defines a minimum operation that takes two elements and returns the lesser of the two.
explanatories.Subtype.prop: This theorem asserts that for a specific subtype, the property defining the subtype holds when applied to its element.
explanatories.le_of_lt: This theorem asserts that if one element is strictly less than another in a preorder, then it is also less than or equal to that element.
explanatories.Fact.out: This theorem asserts that the property represented by a fact can be retrieved from its corresponding instance.
explanatories.imp_self: If a proposition is true, then it implies itself and is equivalent to the truth of any statement.
explanatories.sub_lt_sub_iff_right: This theorem indicates that the condition of subtracting a common element from two elements preserves the inequality if and only if the original elements themselves maintain that inequality in an additive group structure.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element belongs to the set defined by a property if and only if that property holds for the element.
explanatories.forall_true_iff: This theorem establishes that if any element of a type implies a true proposition, it is equivalent to stating that a true proposition is always true.
explanatories.min_lt_iff: An element is less than the minimum of two others if and only if it is less than at least one of those two elements.
explanatories.Set.mem_Icc: This theorem states that an element belongs to the closed interval defined by two given elements in a preorder structure if and only if it is greater than or equal to the first element and less than or equal to the second element.
explanatories.min_eq_left: This theorem states that if one element is less than or equal to another in a linear order, then the minimum of the two elements is equal to the lesser element.
explanatories.sub_add_cancel: In an additive group, subtracting an element from another and then adding the subtracted element back yields the original element.
explanatories.funext: If two functions yield the same output for every input, then those functions are considered equal.
explanatories.Subsingleton.elim: In a subsingleton type, any two elements are equal, demonstrating the uniqueness of elements in such types.
explanatories.add_comm: This theorem asserts that the addition operation in a commutative magma is commutative, meaning the sum of two elements does not depend on the order in which they are added.
explanatories.add_sub_cancel_left: In an additive commutative group, subtracting an element from the sum of that element with another results in the other element.
explanatories.isOpen_Iio: This theorem asserts that in a linear ordered topological space with a closed upper interval topology, the set of all elements strictly less than a given element is an open set.
explanatories.IsOpen.preimage: The preimage of an open set under a continuous function is also an open set.
explanatories.Continuous.continuousOn: If a function is continuous on its entire domain, it is also continuous on any subset of that domain.
explanatories.Continuous.sub: The quotient of two continuous functions in a topological space, when appropriately defined, is also a continuous function.
explanatories.Continuous.add: The pointwise multiplication of two continuous functions from a topological space to a space with a continuous multiplication structure is itself continuous.
explanatories.Continuous.min: This theorem states that if two functions are continuous, then their pointwise minimum is also continuous in a topological space with an order topology.
explanatories.ContDiff.add: The theorem confirms that the sum of two functions, each continuously differentiable to a certain order, is also continuously differentiable to that same order.

IccLeftChart.fullDefinition: def IccLeftChart (x y : ℝ) [h : Fact (x < y)] :     PartialHomeomorph (Icc x y) (EuclideanHalfSpace 1) where   source := { z : Icc x y | z.val < y }   target := { z : EuclideanHalfSpace 1 | z.val 0 < y - x }   toFun := fun z : Icc x y => ⟨fun _ => z.val - x, sub_nonneg.mpr z.property.1⟩   invFun z := ⟨min (z.val 0 + x) y, by simp [le_refl, z.prop, le_of_lt h.out]⟩   map_source' := by simp only [imp_self, sub_lt_sub_iff_right, mem_setOf_eq, forall_true_iff]   map_target' := by     simp only [min_lt_iff, mem_setOf_eq]; intro z hz; left     linarith   left_inv' := by     rintro ⟨z, hz⟩ h'z     simp only [mem_setOf_eq, mem_Icc] at hz h'z     simp only [hz, min_eq_left, sub_add_cancel]   right_inv' := by     rintro ⟨z, hz⟩ h'z     rw [Subtype.mk_eq_mk]     funext i     dsimp at hz h'z     have A : x + z 0 ≤ y := by linarith     rw [Subsingleton.elim i 0]     simp only [A, add_comm, add_sub_cancel_left, min_eq_left]   open_source :=     haveI : IsOpen { z : ℝ | z < y } := isOpen_Iio     this.preimage continuous_subtype_val   open_target := by     have : IsOpen { z : ℝ | z < y - x } := isOpen_Iio     have : IsOpen { z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) | z 0 < y - x } :=       this.preimage (@continuous_apply (Fin 1) (fun _ => ℝ) _ 0)     exact this.preimage continuous_subtype_val   continuousOn_toFun := by     apply Continuous.continuousOn     apply Continuous.subtype_mk     have : Continuous fun (z : ℝ) (_ : Fin 1) => z - x :=       Continuous.sub (continuous_pi fun _ => continuous_id) continuous_const     exact this.comp continuous_subtype_val   continuousOn_invFun := by     apply Continuous.continuousOn     apply Continuous.subtype_mk     have A : Continuous fun z : ℝ => min (z + x) y :=       (continuous_id.add continuous_const).min continuous_const     have B : Continuous fun z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) => z 0 := continuous_apply 0     exact (A.comp B).comp continuous_subtype_val
IccLeftChart.description: This definition describes a partial homeomorphism that represents the left chart for a closed interval on the real line, mapping it to a Euclidean half-space while sending the left endpoint to the origin.

Icc_left_chart.code: IccLeftChart (x y : ℝ) [h : Fact (x < y)] : PartialHomeomorph (↑(Icc x y)) (EuclideanHalfSpace 1)
Icc_left_chart.comment:
The left chart for the topological space `[x, y]`, defined on `[x,y)` and sending `x` to `0` in
`EuclideanHalfSpace 1`.

IccRightChart.fullDefinition: def IccRightChart (x y : ℝ) [h : Fact (x < y)] :     PartialHomeomorph (Icc x y) (EuclideanHalfSpace 1) where   source := { z : Icc x y | x < z.val }   target := { z : EuclideanHalfSpace 1 | z.val 0 < y - x }   toFun z := ⟨fun _ => y - z.val, sub_nonneg.mpr z.property.2⟩   invFun z :=     ⟨max (y - z.val 0) x, by simp [le_refl, z.prop, le_of_lt h.out, sub_eq_add_neg]⟩   map_source' := by simp only [imp_self, mem_setOf_eq, sub_lt_sub_iff_left, forall_true_iff]   map_target' := by     simp only [lt_max_iff, mem_setOf_eq]; intro z hz; left     linarith   left_inv' := by     rintro ⟨z, hz⟩ h'z     simp only [mem_setOf_eq, mem_Icc] at hz h'z     simp only [hz, sub_eq_add_neg, max_eq_left, add_add_neg_cancel'_right, neg_add_rev, neg_neg]   right_inv' := by     rintro ⟨z, hz⟩ h'z     rw [Subtype.mk_eq_mk]     funext i     dsimp at hz h'z     have A : x ≤ y - z 0 := by linarith     rw [Subsingleton.elim i 0]     simp only [A, sub_sub_cancel, max_eq_left]   open_source :=     haveI : IsOpen { z : ℝ | x < z } := isOpen_Ioi     this.preimage continuous_subtype_val   open_target := by     have : IsOpen { z : ℝ | z < y - x } := isOpen_Iio     have : IsOpen { z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) | z 0 < y - x } :=       this.preimage (@continuous_apply (Fin 1) (fun _ => ℝ) _ 0)     exact this.preimage continuous_subtype_val   continuousOn_toFun := by     apply Continuous.continuousOn     apply Continuous.subtype_mk     have : Continuous fun (z : ℝ) (_ : Fin 1) => y - z :=       continuous_const.sub (continuous_pi fun _ => continuous_id)     exact this.comp continuous_subtype_val   continuousOn_invFun := by     apply Continuous.continuousOn     apply Continuous.subtype_mk     have A : Continuous fun z : ℝ => max (y - z) x :=       (continuous_const.sub continuous_id).max continuous_const     have B : Continuous fun z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) => z 0 := continuous_apply 0     exact (A.comp B).comp continuous_subtype_val

explanatories.sub_eq_add_neg: Subtracting an element from another is equivalent to adding the negative of that element.
explanatories.sub_lt_sub_iff_left: This theorem states that in an additive group, the difference between a fixed element and two other elements is less than if and only if the second of those elements is less than the first.

Icc_right_chart.fullDefinition: def IccRightChart (x y : ℝ) [h : Fact (x < y)] :     PartialHomeomorph (Icc x y) (EuclideanHalfSpace 1) where   source := { z : Icc x y | x < z.val }   target := { z : EuclideanHalfSpace 1 | z.val 0 < y - x }   toFun z := ⟨fun _ => y - z.val, sub_nonneg.mpr z.property.2⟩   invFun z :=     ⟨max (y - z.val 0) x, by simp [le_refl, z.prop, le_of_lt h.out, sub_eq_add_neg]⟩   map_source' := by simp only [imp_self, mem_setOf_eq, sub_lt_sub_iff_left, forall_true_iff]   map_target' := by     simp only [lt_max_iff, mem_setOf_eq]; intro z hz; left     linarith   left_inv' := by     rintro ⟨z, hz⟩ h'z     simp only [mem_setOf_eq, mem_Icc] at hz h'z     simp only [hz, sub_eq_add_neg, max_eq_left, add_add_neg_cancel'_right, neg_add_rev, neg_neg]   right_inv' := by     rintro ⟨z, hz⟩ h'z     rw [Subtype.mk_eq_mk]     funext i     dsimp at hz h'z     have A : x ≤ y - z 0 := by linarith     rw [Subsingleton.elim i 0]     simp only [A, sub_sub_cancel, max_eq_left]   open_source :=     haveI : IsOpen { z : ℝ | x < z } := isOpen_Ioi     this.preimage continuous_subtype_val   open_target := by     have : IsOpen { z : ℝ | z < y - x } := isOpen_Iio     have : IsOpen { z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) | z 0 < y - x } :=       this.preimage (@continuous_apply (Fin 1) (fun _ => ℝ) _ 0)     exact this.preimage continuous_subtype_val   continuousOn_toFun := by     apply Continuous.continuousOn     apply Continuous.subtype_mk     have : Continuous fun (z : ℝ) (_ : Fin 1) => y - z :=       continuous_const.sub (continuous_pi fun _ => continuous_id)     exact this.comp continuous_subtype_val   continuousOn_invFun := by     apply Continuous.continuousOn     apply Continuous.subtype_mk     have A : Continuous fun z : ℝ => max (y - z) x :=       (continuous_const.sub continuous_id).max continuous_const     have B : Continuous fun z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) => z 0 := continuous_apply 0     exact (A.comp B).comp continuous_subtype_val

IccManifold.fullDefinition: instance IccManifold (x y : ℝ) [h : Fact (x < y)] :     ChartedSpace (EuclideanHalfSpace 1) (Icc x y) where   atlas := {IccLeftChart x y, IccRightChart x y}   chartAt z := if z.val < y then IccLeftChart x y else IccRightChart x y   mem_chart_source z := by     by_cases h' : z.val < y     · simp only [h', if_true]       exact h'     · simp only [h', if_false]       apply lt_of_lt_of_le h.out       simpa only [not_lt] using h'   chart_mem_atlas z := by by_cases h' : (z : ℝ) < y <;> simp [h']

explanatories.ContDiff.neg: The theorem states that the negative of a continuously differentiable function retains the same order of differentiability.
explanatories.ContDiff.add: The theorem confirms that the sum of two functions, each continuously differentiable to a certain order, is also continuously differentiable to that same order.
explanatories.contDiff_const: The theorem states that a constant function is continuously differentiable to any order in the context of non-trivially normed fields and normed spaces.

explanatories.Set.mem_singleton_iff: An element belongs to a singleton set if and only if it is equal to the unique element in that set.
explanatories.Set.mem_insert_iff: An element belongs to the insertion of an element into a set if and only if it is either that element or an element of the original set.
explanatories.mem_groupoid_of_pregroupoid: A partial homeomorphism is a member of a groupoid constructed from a pregroupoid if and only if it satisfies specific properties related to its source and the properties of its inverse.
explanatories.symm_trans_mem_contDiffGroupoid: The theorem establishes that the composition of a partial homeomorphism and its inverse is contained within the group of continuously differentiable mappings of a specified order associated with a given model with corners.
explanatories.ContDiff.contDiffOn: If a function is continuously differentiable up to a certain order everywhere, then it is also continuously differentiable up to that order on any specific set.
explanatories.ContDiffOn.congr: If a function is continuously differentiable on a set, then another function that is equal to the first function at all points in that set is also continuously differentiable on the same set.

Icc_smooth_manifold.fullDefinition: instance Icc_smooth_manifold (x y : ℝ) [Fact (x < y)] :     SmoothManifoldWithCorners (𝓡∂ 1) (Icc x y) := by   have M : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (show EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)       from fun z i => -z i + (y - x)) :=     contDiff_id.neg.add contDiff_const   apply smoothManifoldWithCorners_of_contDiffOn   intro e e' he he'   simp only [atlas, mem_singleton_iff, mem_insert_iff] at he he'   /- We need to check that any composition of two charts gives a `C^∞` function. Each chart can be   either the left chart or the right chart, leaving 4 possibilities that we handle successively. -/   rcases he with (rfl | rfl) <;> rcases he' with (rfl | rfl)   · -- `e = left chart`, `e' = left chart`     exact (mem_groupoid_of_pregroupoid.mpr (symm_trans_mem_contDiffGroupoid _ _ _)).1   · -- `e = left chart`, `e' = right chart`     apply M.contDiffOn.congr     rintro _ ⟨⟨hz₁, hz₂⟩, ⟨⟨z, hz₀⟩, rfl⟩⟩     simp only [modelWithCornersEuclideanHalfSpace, IccLeftChart, IccRightChart, update_same,       max_eq_left, hz₀, lt_sub_iff_add_lt, mfld_simps] at hz₁ hz₂     rw [min_eq_left hz₁.le, lt_add_iff_pos_left] at hz₂     ext i     rw [Subsingleton.elim i 0]     simp only [modelWithCornersEuclideanHalfSpace, IccLeftChart, IccRightChart, *, PiLp.add_apply,       PiLp.neg_apply, max_eq_left, min_eq_left hz₁.le, update_same, mfld_simps]     abel   · -- `e = right chart`, `e' = left chart`     apply M.contDiffOn.congr     rintro _ ⟨⟨hz₁, hz₂⟩, ⟨z, hz₀⟩, rfl⟩     simp only [modelWithCornersEuclideanHalfSpace, IccLeftChart, IccRightChart, max_lt_iff,       update_same, max_eq_left hz₀, mfld_simps] at hz₁ hz₂     rw [lt_sub_comm] at hz₁     ext i     rw [Subsingleton.elim i 0]     simp only [modelWithCornersEuclideanHalfSpace, IccLeftChart, IccRightChart, PiLp.add_apply,       PiLp.neg_apply, update_same, max_eq_left, hz₀, hz₁.le, mfld_simps]     abel   ·-- `e = right chart`, `e' = right chart`     exact (mem_groupoid_of_pregroupoid.mpr (symm_trans_mem_contDiffGroupoid _ _ _)).1

stereoToFun.comment:

stereoInvFunAux.comment:
Auxiliary function for the construction of the reverse direction of the stereographic
projection.  This is a map from the orthogonal complement of a unit vector `v` in an inner product
space `E` to `E`; we will later prove that it takes values in the unit sphere.

For most purposes, use `stereoInvFun`, not `stereoInvFunAux`.
stereoInvFunAux.fullDefinition: def stereoInvFunAux (w : E) : E :=   (‖w‖ ^ 2 + 4)⁻¹ • ((4 : ℝ) • w + (‖w‖ ^ 2 - 4) • v)

stereographic.fullDefinition: def stereographic (hv : ‖v‖ = 1) : PartialHomeomorph (sphere (0 : E) 1) (ℝ ∙ v)ᗮ where   toFun := stereoToFun v ∘ (↑)   invFun := stereoInvFun hv   source := {⟨v, by simp [hv]⟩}ᶜ   target := Set.univ   map_source' := by simp   map_target' {w} _ := fun h => (stereoInvFun_ne_north_pole hv w) (Set.eq_of_mem_singleton h)   left_inv' x hx := stereo_left_inv hv fun h => hx (by     rw [← h] at hv     apply Subtype.ext     dsimp     exact h)   right_inv' w _ := stereo_right_inv hv w   open_source := isOpen_compl_singleton   open_target := isOpen_univ   continuousOn_toFun :=     continuousOn_stereoToFun.comp continuous_subtype_val.continuousOn fun w h => by       dsimp       exact         h ∘ Subtype.ext ∘ Eq.symm ∘ (inner_eq_one_iff_of_norm_one hv (by simp)).mp   continuousOn_invFun := (continuous_stereoInvFun hv).continuousOn

explanatories.Ne: The inequality between two elements is defined by the negation of their equality, asserting that they are distinct.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff: The theorem asserts that any continuous linear map is continuously differentiable to any order within the context of non-trivially normed fields and normed spaces.
explanatories.ContDiff.contDiffOn: If a function is continuously differentiable up to a certain order everywhere, then it is also continuously differentiable up to that order on any specific set.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.contDiffOn_stereoToFun: This theorem asserts that the stereographic projection map is continuously differentiable on the set of points in an inner product space where the inner product with a given vector is not equal to one.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.id: The identity map on a module over a semiring is defined as a continuous linear map that maps every element to itself.
explanatories.RingHom.id: This definition describes the identity ring homomorphism that maps each element of a semiring to itself.
explanatories.HasFDerivAt.comp: If a function has a derivative at a point and another function has a derivative at the image of that point, then the composition of these functions also has a derivative at that point with the appropriately derived composition, illustrating the chain rule.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.contDiff_stereoInvFunAux: This theorem asserts that the auxiliary function used in the inverse stereographic projection is continuously differentiable in all dimensions.
explanatories.real_inner_comm: This theorem asserts that the inner product of two elements in a real inner product space is symmetric, meaning it gives the same result regardless of the order of the elements.
explanatories.Continuous.comp: The composition of two continuous functions in topological spaces is itself continuous.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.ContinuousOn.comp: The composition of two continuous functions, where the output of the first function maps into the domain of the second, is itself continuous on the specified set of the first function.
explanatories.OrthonormalBasis.fromOrthogonalSpanSingl: This definition asserts that for a finite-dimensional inner product space, there exists an orthonormal basis of a vector space that is the orthogonal complement of a non-zero vector, specifically when the space's rank is one greater than a specified natural number.
explanatories.ne_zero_of_mem_unit_sphere: The theorem asserts that any element located on a unit sphere in a seminormed group cannot be equal to the identity element.
explanatories.OrthonormalBasis.repr: This definition establishes a linear isometry between an inner product space and a Euclidean space that corresponds to an orthonormal basis.
explanatories.stereographic'_source: This theorem states that the source of the n-dimensional stereographic projection from a unit sphere excludes a specific point.
explanatories.stereographic'_target: This theorem establishes that the target of a specific stereographic projection map, defined for a given dimension of a vector space and applied to a point on the unit sphere, is the entire space.
explanatories.sphere_ext_iff: This theorem states that two points on the unit sphere are equal if and only if their inner product is equal to one.
explanatories.stereographic'_symm_apply: This theorem specifies the expression for the inverse stereographic projection of a point in a Euclidean space onto a sphere, incorporating a transformation based on an orthonormal basis.
explanatories.smoothManifoldWithCorners_of_contDiffOn: This theorem shows that a manifold can be constructed with corners by ensuring that certain composition maps between atlas charts exhibit continuous differentiability on the defined sets.
explanatories.LinearIsometryEquiv.contDiff: The theorem establishes that any linear isometry equivalence between normed spaces is continuously differentiable to any order in the context of non-trivially normed fields.
explanatories.ContDiff.comp_contDiffOn: The theorem states that the composition of a continuously differentiable function up to a specified order with another continuously differentiable function defined on a domain also yields a function that is continuously differentiable on that domain to the same order.
explanatories.ContDiff.comp: The theorem states that the composition of two continuously differentiable functions, each differentiable up to a specified order, is also continuously differentiable to the same order.
explanatories.ContDiffOn.comp': The theorem states that the composition of two continuously differentiable functions on their respective domains results in a function that is also continuously differentiable on the intersection of those domains.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.trans_toPartialEquiv: This theorem confirms the equality between the composition of two partial homeomorphisms as a partial equivalence and the direct composition of their respective partial equivalences.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.symm_toPartialEquiv: This theorem establishes that the inverse of a partial homeomorphism, when viewed as a partial equivalence, is equal to its corresponding inverse.
explanatories.PartialEquiv.trans_source: This theorem states that the source of the composition of two partial equivalences is equal to the intersection of the original source and the preimage of the source of the second equivalence under the first.
explanatories.PartialEquiv.symm_source: This theorem asserts that the source set of the inverse of a partial equivalence is equal to the target set of the original partial equivalence.
explanatories.modelWithCornersSelf_coe: This theorem states that the canonical embedding of a model with corners from a field to a normed space is the identity function.
explanatories.modelWithCornersSelf_coe_symm: This theorem states that the inverse of a specific model with corners is equivalent to the identity function.
explanatories.Set.preimage_id: The preimage of any set under the identity function is the set itself.
explanatories.Set.range_id: The range of the identity function is the universal set, containing all elements of the given type.
explanatories.Set.inter_univ: The intersection of any set with the universal set is equal to that set.
explanatories.Set.univ_inter: The intersection of the universal set with any set is equal to that set.
explanatories.Set.compl_singleton_eq: The complement of a singleton set is the set of all elements that are not equal to the element in the singleton.
explanatories.Set.preimage_setOf_eq: The preimage of the set of elements satisfying a property under a function is equal to the set of elements in the domain that map to elements satisfying that property.
explanatories.Function.comp_apply: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.
explanatories.Submodule.subtypeL_apply: The theorem confirms that the application of the inclusion map from a submodule to its parent module equals the original element when evaluated at an element of the submodule.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.coe_coe_symm: This theorem asserts that the coercion of the symmetrized version of a partial homeomorphism is equal to itself.
explanatories.innerSL_apply: This theorem shows that applying the inner product in a specific way to two vectors is equivalent to their inner product as defined in the inner product space.
explanatories.ContMDiffOn.comp': This theorem states that if two functions are continuously differentiable to a specified order over their respective domains, then their composition is also continuously differentiable to the same order over the intersection of the domain of the first function and the pre-image of the second function's domain.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.ContMDiff.comp: This theorem states that the composition of two functions, each of which is continuously differentiable to a specified order across their respective domains, is also continuously differentiable to the same order across the domain of the composed function.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearEquiv.contDiff: The theorem asserts that a continuous linear equivalence between two normed spaces is continuously differentiable to any order within the framework of non-trivially normed fields and normed spaces.

EuclideanSpace.instSmoothManifoldWithCor.fullDefinition: instance EuclideanSpace.instSmoothManifoldWithCornersSphere {n : ℕ} [Fact (finrank ℝ E = n + 1)] :     SmoothManifoldWithCorners (𝓡 n) (sphere (0 : E) 1) :=   smoothManifoldWithCorners_of_contDiffOn (𝓡 n) (sphere (0 : E) 1)     (by       rintro _ _ ⟨v, rfl⟩ ⟨v', rfl⟩       let U :=         (-- Removed type ascription, and this helped for some reason with timeout issues?             OrthonormalBasis.fromOrthogonalSpanSingleton (𝕜 := ℝ)             n (ne_zero_of_mem_unit_sphere v)).repr       let U' :=         (-- Removed type ascription, and this helped for some reason with timeout issues?             OrthonormalBasis.fromOrthogonalSpanSingleton (𝕜 := ℝ)             n (ne_zero_of_mem_unit_sphere v')).repr       have H₁ := U'.contDiff.comp_contDiffOn contDiffOn_stereoToFun       -- Porting note: need to help with implicit variables again       have H₂ := (contDiff_stereoInvFunAux (v := v.val)|>.comp         (ℝ ∙ (v : E))ᗮ.subtypeL.contDiff).comp U.symm.contDiff       convert H₁.comp' (H₂.contDiffOn : ContDiffOn ℝ ⊤ _ Set.univ) using 1       -- -- squeezed from `ext, simp [sphere_ext_iff, stereographic'_symm_apply, real_inner_comm]`       simp only [PartialHomeomorph.trans_toPartialEquiv, PartialHomeomorph.symm_toPartialEquiv,         PartialEquiv.trans_source, PartialEquiv.symm_source, stereographic'_target,         stereographic'_source]       simp only [modelWithCornersSelf_coe, modelWithCornersSelf_coe_symm, Set.preimage_id,         Set.range_id, Set.inter_univ, Set.univ_inter, Set.compl_singleton_eq, Set.preimage_setOf_eq]       simp only [id, comp_apply, Submodule.subtypeL_apply, PartialHomeomorph.coe_coe_symm,         innerSL_apply, Ne, sphere_ext_iff, real_inner_comm (v' : E)]       rfl)
EuclideanSpace.instSmoothManifoldWithCor.description: This definition establishes that the unit sphere in an \(n + 1\)-dimensional inner product space forms a smooth manifold modeled on \(n\)-dimensional Euclidean space.

linear map from `TangentSpace (𝓡 n) v` to `E`.  The range of this map is the orthogonal complement

analyticGroupoid.comment:

as the maps that are analytic and map interior to interior when read in `E` through `I`. We also
explicitly define that they are `C^∞` on the whole domain, since we are only requiring
analyticity on the interior of the domain.

analyticGroupoid.description: This definition establishes a groupoid of analytic transformations for a given model with corners, consisting of maps that are analytic on the interior and smooth throughout their entire domain.

analyticGroupoid.eq_1.code:
analyticGroupoid.eq_1.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H) :
  analyticGroupoid I =
    contDiffGroupoid ⊤ I ⊓
      {
          property := fun f s =>
            AnalyticOn 𝕜 (↑I ∘ f ∘ ↑I.symm) (↑I.symm ⁻¹' s ∩ interior (range ↑I)) ∧
              ↑I ∘ f ∘ ↑I.symm '' (↑I.symm ⁻¹' s ∩ interior (range ↑I)) ⊆ interior (range ↑I),
          comp := ⋯, id_mem := ⋯, locality := ⋯, congr := ⋯ }.groupoid

FiberwiseLinear.partialHomeomorph.fullDefinition: def partialHomeomorph (φ : B → F ≃L[𝕜] F) (hU : IsOpen U)     (hφ : ContinuousOn (fun x => φ x : B → F →L[𝕜] F) U)     (h2φ : ContinuousOn (fun x => (φ x).symm : B → F →L[𝕜] F) U) :     PartialHomeomorph (B × F) (B × F) where   toFun x := (x.1, φ x.1 x.2)   invFun x := (x.1, (φ x.1).symm x.2)   source := U ×ˢ univ   target := U ×ˢ univ   map_source' _x hx := mk_mem_prod hx.1 (mem_univ _)   map_target' _x hx := mk_mem_prod hx.1 (mem_univ _)   left_inv' _ _ := Prod.ext rfl (ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply _ _)   right_inv' _ _ := Prod.ext rfl (ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply _ _)   open_source := hU.prod isOpen_univ   open_target := hU.prod isOpen_univ   continuousOn_toFun :=     have : ContinuousOn (fun p : B × F => ((φ p.1 : F →L[𝕜] F), p.2)) (U ×ˢ univ) :=       hφ.prod_map continuousOn_id     continuousOn_fst.prod (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply.continuous.comp_continuousOn this)   continuousOn_invFun :=     haveI : ContinuousOn (fun p : B × F => (((φ p.1).symm : F →L[𝕜] F), p.2)) (U ×ˢ univ) :=       h2φ.prod_map continuousOn_id     continuousOn_fst.prod (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply.continuous.comp_continuousOn this)

SmoothFiberwiseLinear.locality_aux₁.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {B : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3}
  [TopologicalSpace B] [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] {EB : Type u_4}
  [NormedAddCommGroup EB] [NormedSpace 𝕜 EB] {HB : Type u_5} [TopologicalSpace HB] [ChartedSpace HB B]
  {IB : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 EB HB} (e : PartialHomeomorph (B × F) (B × F))
  (h :
    ∀ p ∈ e.source,
      ∃ s,
        IsOpen s ∧
          p ∈ s ∧
            ∃ φ u,
              ∃ (hu : IsOpen u) (hφ : SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F) (fun x => ↑(φ x)) u) (h2φ :
                SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F) (fun x => ↑(φ x).symm) u),
                (e.restr s).EqOnSource (FiberwiseLinear.partialHomeomorph φ hu ⋯ ⋯)) :
  ∃ U,
    e.source = U ×ˢ univ ∧
      ∀ x ∈ U,
        ∃ φ u,
          ∃ (hu : IsOpen u) (_ : u ⊆ U) (_ : x ∈ u) (hφ : SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F) (fun x => ↑(φ x)) u) (h2φ :
            SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F) (fun x => ↑(φ x).symm) u),
            (e.restr (u ×ˢ univ)).EqOnSource (FiberwiseLinear.partialHomeomorph φ hu ⋯ ⋯)
SmoothFiberwiseLinear.locality_aux₁.comment:
Let `e` be a partial homeomorphism of `B × F`.  Suppose that at every point `p` in the source of
`e`, there is some neighbourhood `s` of `p` on which `e` is equal to a bi-smooth fiberwise linear
partial homeomorphism.
Then the source of `e` is of the form `U ×ˢ univ`, for some set `U` in `B`, and, at any point `x` in
`U`, admits a neighbourhood `u` of `x` such that `e` is equal on `u ×ˢ univ` to some bi-smooth
fiberwise linear partial homeomorphism.

SmoothFiberwiseLinear.locality_aux₂.code:
SmoothFiberwiseLinear.locality_aux₂.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {B : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3}
  [TopologicalSpace B] [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] {EB : Type u_4}
  [NormedAddCommGroup EB] [NormedSpace 𝕜 EB] {HB : Type u_5} [TopologicalSpace HB] [ChartedSpace HB B]
  {IB : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 EB HB} (e : PartialHomeomorph (B × F) (B × F)) (U : Set B) (hU : e.source = U ×ˢ univ)
  (h :
    ∀ x ∈ U,
      ∃ φ u,
        ∃ (hu : IsOpen u) (_ : u ⊆ U) (_ : x ∈ u) (hφ : SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F) (fun x => ↑(φ x)) u) (h2φ :
          SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F) (fun x => ↑(φ x).symm) u),
          (e.restr (u ×ˢ univ)).EqOnSource (FiberwiseLinear.partialHomeomorph φ hu ⋯ ⋯)) :
  ∃ Φ U,
    ∃ (hU₀ : IsOpen U) (hΦ : SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F) (fun x => ↑(Φ x)) U) (h2Φ :
      SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F) (fun x => ↑(Φ x).symm) U), e.EqOnSource (FiberwiseLinear.partialHomeomorph Φ hU₀ ⋯ ⋯)
SmoothFiberwiseLinear.locality_aux₂.comment:
Let `e` be a partial homeomorphism of `B × F` whose source is `U ×ˢ univ`, for some set `U` in
`B`, and which, at any point `x` in `U`, admits a neighbourhood `u` of `x` such that `e` is equal
on `u ×ˢ univ` to some bi-smooth fiberwise linear partial homeomorphism.  Then `e` itself
is equal to some bi-smooth fiberwise linear partial homeomorphism.

This is the key mathematical point of the `locality` condition in the construction of the
`StructureGroupoid` of bi-smooth fiberwise linear partial homeomorphisms.  The proof is by gluing
together the various bi-smooth fiberwise linear partial homeomorphism which exist locally.

The `U` in the conclusion is the same `U` as in the hypothesis. We state it like this, because this
is exactly what we need for `smoothFiberwiseLinear`.

smoothFiberwiseLinear.comment:
For `B` a manifold and `F` a normed space, the groupoid on `B × F` consisting of local
homeomorphisms which are bi-smooth and fiberwise linear, and induce the identity on `B`.
When a (topological) vector bundle is smooth, then the composition of charts associated
to the vector bundle belong to this groupoid.
