smoothFiberwiseLinear.fullDefinition: def smoothFiberwiseLinear : StructureGroupoid (B × F) where   members :=     ⋃ (φ : B → F ≃L[𝕜] F) (U : Set B) (hU : IsOpen U)       (hφ : SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F) (fun x => φ x : B → F →L[𝕜] F) U)       (h2φ : SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F) (fun x => (φ x).symm : B → F →L[𝕜] F) U),         {e | e.EqOnSource (FiberwiseLinear.partialHomeomorph φ hU hφ.continuousOn h2φ.continuousOn)}   trans' := by     simp only [mem_aux]     rintro e e' ⟨φ, U, hU, hφ, h2φ, heφ⟩ ⟨φ', U', hU', hφ', h2φ', heφ'⟩     refine ⟨fun b => (φ b).trans (φ' b), _, hU.inter hU', ?_, ?_,       Setoid.trans (PartialHomeomorph.EqOnSource.trans' heφ heφ') ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩     · show         SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F)           (fun x : B => (φ' x).toContinuousLinearMap ∘L (φ x).toContinuousLinearMap) (U ∩ U')       exact (hφ'.mono inter_subset_right).clm_comp (hφ.mono inter_subset_left)     · show         SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F)           (fun x : B => (φ x).symm.toContinuousLinearMap ∘L (φ' x).symm.toContinuousLinearMap)           (U ∩ U')       exact (h2φ.mono inter_subset_left).clm_comp (h2φ'.mono inter_subset_right)     · apply FiberwiseLinear.source_trans_partialHomeomorph     · rintro ⟨b, v⟩ -; apply FiberwiseLinear.trans_partialHomeomorph_apply   -- Porting note: without introducing `e` first, the first `simp only` fails   symm' := fun e ↦ by     simp only [mem_aux]     rintro ⟨φ, U, hU, hφ, h2φ, heφ⟩     refine ⟨fun b => (φ b).symm, U, hU, h2φ, ?_, PartialHomeomorph.EqOnSource.symm' heφ⟩     simp_rw [ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm_symm]     exact hφ   id_mem' := by     simp_rw [mem_aux]     refine ⟨fun _ ↦ ContinuousLinearEquiv.refl 𝕜 F, univ, isOpen_univ, smoothOn_const,       smoothOn_const, ⟨?_, fun b _hb ↦ rfl⟩⟩     simp only [FiberwiseLinear.partialHomeomorph, PartialHomeomorph.refl_partialEquiv,       PartialEquiv.refl_source, univ_prod_univ]   locality' := by     -- the hard work has been extracted to `locality_aux₁` and `locality_aux₂`     simp only [mem_aux]     intro e he     obtain ⟨U, hU, h⟩ := SmoothFiberwiseLinear.locality_aux₁ e he     exact SmoothFiberwiseLinear.locality_aux₂ e U hU h   mem_of_eqOnSource' := by     simp only [mem_aux]     rintro e e' ⟨φ, U, hU, hφ, h2φ, heφ⟩ hee'     exact ⟨φ, U, hU, hφ, h2φ, Setoid.trans hee' heφ⟩
smoothFiberwiseLinear.description: This definition describes a groupoid on the product of a manifold and a normed space, consisting of local homeomorphisms that are both bi-smooth and fiberwise linear while maintaining the identity on the manifold.

smooth_fiberwise_linear.code:
smoothFiberwiseLinear.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {𝕜 : Type u_1} (B : Type u_2) (F : Type u_3) [TopologicalSpace B]
  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] {EB : Type u_4} [NormedAddCommGroup EB]
  [NormedSpace 𝕜 EB] {HB : Type u_5} [TopologicalSpace HB] [ChartedSpace HB B] (IB : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 EB HB) :
  StructureGroupoid (B × F)
smooth_fiberwise_linear.comment:
For `B` a manifold and `F` a normed space, the groupoid on `B × F` consisting of local
homeomorphisms which are bi-smooth and fiberwise linear, and induce the identity on `B`.
When a (topological) vector bundle is smooth, then the composition of charts associated
to the vector bundle belong to this groupoid.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm: The inverse of a continuous linear equivalence between two modules also forms a continuous linear equivalence between those modules.
explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.FiberwiseLinear.partialHomeomorph: This definition establishes that a continuous map from an open subset of a topological space to a linear equivalence in a normed space induces a partial homeomorphism on the product of the topological space and the normed space.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.trans: This definition describes how to create a new partial homeomorphism by composing two existing partial homeomorphisms, limited to the domain where their composition is valid.
explanatories.FiberwiseLinear.trans_partialHomeomorph_: The theorem demonstrates that the composition of two partial homeomorphisms, each induced by fiberwise linear equivalences, can be computed by applying these equivalences sequentially to an element in their respective domains.

explanatories.FiberwiseLinear.source_trans_partialHome: The theorem shows that the source of the composition of two partial homeomorphisms, each induced by fiberwise linear equivalences, is given by the intersection of their open sets along with the universal set for the normed space.

explanatories.ContMDiffOn.continuousOn: This theorem asserts that if a function is continuously differentiable to a specified order on a set within a manifold, then it is also continuous on that set.

explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.SmoothFiberwiseLinear.locality_aux₁: If a partial homeomorphism defined on a product space is locally equivalent to a bi-smooth fiberwise linear partial homeomorphism around every point in its source, then its source can be expressed as a product of an open set in the first component and the universal set in the second component.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearEquiv.refl: The identity map on a topological module is defined as a continuous linear equivalence between the module and itself.
explanatories.ContMDiffOn.mono: This theorem states that if a function is continuously differentiable on a larger set, then it remains continuously differentiable on any subset of that set.
explanatories.Set.inter_subset_right: The intersection of two sets is a subset of the second set.
explanatories.SmoothFiberwiseLinear.locality_aux₂: If a partial homeomorphism defined on the product space has a source expressed as a product of a set and the universal set, and if at each point in this set it locally resembles a bi-smooth fiberwise linear partial homeomorphism, then it can be globally represented as some bi-smooth fiberwise linear partial homeomorphism.

mem_smoothFiberwiseLinear_iff.code:
mem_smoothFiberwiseLinear_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {𝕜 : Type u_1} (B : Type u_2) (F : Type u_3)
  [TopologicalSpace B] [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] {EB : Type u_4}
  [NormedAddCommGroup EB] [NormedSpace 𝕜 EB] {HB : Type u_5} [TopologicalSpace HB] [ChartedSpace HB B]
  (IB : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 EB HB) (e : PartialHomeomorph (B × F) (B × F)) :
  e ∈ smoothFiberwiseLinear B F IB ↔
    ∃ φ U,
      ∃ (hU : IsOpen U) (hφ : SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F) (fun x => ↑(φ x)) U) (h2φ :
        SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F) (fun x => ↑(φ x).symm) U), e.EqOnSource (FiberwiseLinear.partialHomeomorph φ hU ⋯ ⋯)

FiberBundle.chartedSpace'.comment:
A fiber bundle `E` over a base `B` with model fiber `F` is naturally a charted space modelled on
`B × F`.

explanatories.Trivialization.toPartialHomeomorph: A trivialization establishes a structure that creates a partial homeomorphism between a given space and the product of its base space with its fiber.
explanatories.FiberBundle.trivializationAtlas: This defines a set of local trivializations that form an atlas for a fiber bundle over a given base space.
explanatories.Trivialization.mem_source: An element is in the source of a trivialization if and only if its projection is contained in the base set.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.FiberBundle.mem_baseSet_trivializationAt: Every point in the base space is included in the base set of the corresponding local trivialization for the given fiber bundle.
explanatories.Set.mem_image_of_mem: If an element belongs to a set, then its image under a function belongs to the image of that set.
explanatories.FiberBundle.trivialization_mem_atlas: The local trivialization of a fiber bundle at a given base point is a member of its corresponding trivialization atlas.
explanatories.chartAt: This definition specifies the preferred chart at a given point in a charted space, representing a partial homeomorphism between the manifold and the Euclidean space.

FiberBundle.chartedSpace'.fullDefinition: instance FiberBundle.chartedSpace' : ChartedSpace (B × F) (TotalSpace F E) where   atlas := (fun e : Trivialization F (π F E) => e.toPartialHomeomorph) '' trivializationAtlas F E   chartAt x := (trivializationAt F E x.proj).toPartialHomeomorph   mem_chart_source x :=     (trivializationAt F E x.proj).mem_source.mpr (mem_baseSet_trivializationAt F E x.proj)   chart_mem_atlas _ := mem_image_of_mem _ (trivialization_mem_atlas F E _)

explanatories.ChartedSpace.comp: This definition allows for the combination of two charted spaces, treating one as a chart for the other, thus creating a new charted space.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.ContinuousWithinAt.comp: If a function is continuous at a point within a set and it maps that set into another, then the composition of these functions is also continuous at that point within the first set.
explanatories.StructureGroupoid.HasGroupoid.comp: This theorem asserts that if a structure groupoid is closed under restriction and certain local properties lift under specific morphisms, then the groupoid is also applicable to a higher-dimensional space defined by another structure groupoid.
explanatories.SmoothOn.comp: This theorem states that if two functions are smooth over their respective domains and the range of the first function is contained within the domain of the second function, then their composition is also smooth over the domain of the first function.

SmoothFiberwiseLinear.hasGroupoid.description: The structure of a smooth vector bundle defined over a base space ensures that the transition between any two trivializations is smooth and maintains a fiberwise linear relationship.

explanatories.ChartedSpace.comp: This definition allows for the combination of two charted spaces, treating one as a chart for the other, thus creating a new charted space.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.prod: This definition establishes a way to construct a new partial homeomorphism on the product space by combining two given partial homeomorphisms on individual spaces.
explanatories.ModelWithCorners.prod: This definition specifies how to create a new model with corners on the product of two spaces from existing models with corners on each of those spaces.
explanatories.PartialEquiv.prod: The definition describes the construction of a partial equivalence relating the product of two types to the product of their corresponding partial equivalences.
explanatories.Trivialization.target_eq: The target of a trivialization is equal to the Cartesian product of its base set with the universal space.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.ContinuousWithinAt.comp: If a function is continuous at a point within a set and it maps that set into another, then the composition of these functions is also continuous at that point within the first set.
explanatories.ContMDiffOn.congr: This theorem states that if two functions agree on a set and one is continuously differentiable on that set, then the other function is also continuously differentiable on the same set.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.ContMDiffWithinAt.clm_apply: This theorem states that if two functions are continuously differentiable at a point within a manifold, one being a continuous linear map and the other a function from the manifold to a normed space, then their composition is also continuously differentiable at that point.
explanatories.contMDiffOn_fst: This theorem states that the projection onto the first component of a product space is continuously differentiable on a given set.
explanatories.ContMDiffOn.prod_mk: This theorem states that if two functions are continuously differentiable on a set, then their product function, which maps into the space formed by their Cartesian product, is also continuously differentiable on that set.
explanatories.contMDiffOn_snd: This theorem asserts that the second component of a product function is continuously differentiable on a specified set when the product of the spaces is continuously differentiable in the same context.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.mem_smoothFiberwiseLinear_iff: A partial homeomorphism is considered to be smooth fiberwise linear if and only if there exists a continuously differentiable map and an open set such that the homeomorphism locally resembles a bi-smooth fiberwise linear structure on that set.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.StructureGroupoid.HasGroupoid.comp: This theorem asserts that if a structure groupoid is closed under restriction and certain local properties lift under specific morphisms, then the groupoid is also applicable to a higher-dimensional space defined by another structure groupoid.
explanatories.isLocalStructomorphOn_contDiffGroupoid_i: This theorem states that a partial homeomorphism between two smooth manifolds is a local structomorphism if and only if it is smoothly differentiable in both directions on its respective source and target sets.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.EqOnSource.eqOn: This theorem states that if two partial homeomorphisms are equivalent, then their images coincide on their shared source set.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.EqOnSource.symm': This theorem states that if two partial homeomorphisms are equivalent, then their inverses are also equivalent.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.EqOnSource.source_eq: This theorem demonstrates that if two partial homeomorphisms are equivalent, they must share the same source set.
explanatories.smoothOn_fst: This theorem establishes that if two spaces equipped with models with corners are smooth on a specified set, then the first projection function is also smooth on that set when considered in the context of the product of the two spaces.
explanatories.SmoothOn.prod_mk: This theorem asserts that if two functions are smooth on a specified set, then their product function, which maps into the product space of their target spaces, is also smooth on that set.
explanatories.SmoothOn.comp: This theorem states that if two functions are smooth over their respective domains and the range of the first function is contained within the domain of the second function, then their composition is also smooth over the domain of the first function.
explanatories.Set.prod_subset_preimage_fst: The theorem asserts that the Cartesian product of two sets is a subset of the preimage of the first set under the first projection function.
explanatories.ContMDiffOn.clm_apply: This theorem demonstrates that if two functions are continuously differentiable on a specified set, then their composition, where one function takes as input the output of the other, is also continuously differentiable on that set.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.EqOnSource.target_eq: This theorem states that if two partial homeomorphisms are equivalent, they necessarily have the same target space.

explanatories.ContMDiffAt.coordChangeL: The change of coordinates between two trivializations of a fiber bundle is continuously differentiable at a point if the corresponding smooth map from the manifold to the base of the bundle is also continuously differentiable at that point.
explanatories.ContMDiffOn.coordChangeL: The condition for a function to be continuously differentiable on a specified set can be transformed through a change of coordinates between two trivializations over that set, given that the function maps into the base sets of both trivializations.
explanatories.ContMDiff.coordChangeL: The change of coordinates between two trivializations of a smooth vector bundle is continuously differentiable if the associated smooth map from the manifold to the base space remains within the base sets of both trivializations for all points in the manifold.

explanatories.smooth_const: This theorem states that a constant function defined on a manifold is smooth with respect to the specified smooth structures of the manifolds involved.
explanatories.Smooth.smoothOn: The theorem states that if a function is smooth across its entire domain, then it is also smooth when restricted to any specific subset of that domain.

  (e : Pretrivialization F TotalSpace.proj) :

        SmoothOn IB 𝓘(𝕜, F →L[𝕜] F) f (e.baseSet ∩ e'.baseSet) ∧

tangentBundleCore.code:
tangentBundleCore.{u_1, u_2, u_4, u_6} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H) (M : Type u_6) [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace H M] [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M] : VectorBundleCore 𝕜 M E ↑(atlas H M)
tangentBundleCore.comment:
Let `M` be a smooth manifold with corners with model `I` on `(E, H)`.
Then `VectorBundleCore I M` is the vector bundle core for the tangent bundle over `M`.
It is indexed by the atlas of `M`, with fiber `E` and its change of coordinates from the chart `i`
to the chart `j` at point `x : M` is the derivative of the composite
```
  I.symm   i.symm    j     I
E -----> H -----> M --> H --> E
```
within the set `range I ⊆ E` at `I (i x) : E`.

tangentBundleCore.fullDefinition: def tangentBundleCore : VectorBundleCore 𝕜 M E (atlas H M) where   baseSet i := i.1.source   isOpen_baseSet i := i.1.open_source   indexAt := achart H   mem_baseSet_at := mem_chart_source H   coordChange i j x :=     fderivWithin 𝕜 (j.1.extend I ∘ (i.1.extend I).symm) (range I) (i.1.extend I x)   coordChange_self i x hx v := by     simp only     rw [Filter.EventuallyEq.fderivWithin_eq, fderivWithin_id', ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply]     · exact I.unique_diff_at_image     · filter_upwards [i.1.extend_target_mem_nhdsWithin I hx] with y hy       exact (i.1.extend I).right_inv hy     · simp_rw [Function.comp_apply, i.1.extend_left_inv I hx]   continuousOn_coordChange i j := by     refine (contDiffOn_fderiv_coord_change I i j).continuousOn.comp       ((i.1.continuousOn_extend I).mono ?_) ?_     · rw [i.1.extend_source]; exact inter_subset_left     simp_rw [← i.1.extend_image_source_inter, mapsTo_image]   coordChange_comp := by     rintro i j k x ⟨⟨hxi, hxj⟩, hxk⟩ v     rw [fderivWithin_fderivWithin, Filter.EventuallyEq.fderivWithin_eq]     · have := i.1.extend_preimage_mem_nhds I hxi (j.1.extend_source_mem_nhds I hxj)       filter_upwards [nhdsWithin_le_nhds this] with y hy       simp_rw [Function.comp_apply, (j.1.extend I).left_inv hy]     · simp_rw [Function.comp_apply, i.1.extend_left_inv I hxi, j.1.extend_left_inv I hxj]     · exact (contDiffWithinAt_extend_coord_change' I (subset_maximalAtlas I k.2)         (subset_maximalAtlas I j.2) hxk hxj).differentiableWithinAt le_top     · exact (contDiffWithinAt_extend_coord_change' I (subset_maximalAtlas I j.2)         (subset_maximalAtlas I i.2) hxj hxi).differentiableWithinAt le_top     · intro x _; exact mem_range_self _     · exact I.unique_diff_at_image     · rw [Function.comp_apply, i.1.extend_left_inv I hxi]
tangentBundleCore.description: The definition describes the core of the tangent bundle over a smooth manifold with corners, specifying its structure as a vector bundle indexed by the manifold's atlas and relating fiber coordinates through specified charts.

tangent_bundle_core.code:
tangentBundleCore.{u_1, u_2, u_4, u_6} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H) (M : Type u_6) [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace H M] [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M] : VectorBundleCore 𝕜 M E ↑(atlas H M)
tangent_bundle_core.comment:
Let `M` be a smooth manifold with corners with model `I` on `(E, H)`.
Then `VectorBundleCore I M` is the vector bundle core for the tangent bundle over `M`.
It is indexed by the atlas of `M`, with fiber `E` and its change of coordinates from the chart `i`
to the chart `j` at point `x : M` is the derivative of the composite
```
  I.symm   i.symm    j     I
E -----> H -----> M --> H --> E
```
within the set `range I ⊆ E` at `I (i x) : E`.

explanatories.Function.comp_apply: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.

explanatories.fderivWithin_fderivWithin: The theorem states that if two functions are differentiable within specified sets at certain points, and the first function maps into the domain of the second function while adhering to certain conditions, then the derivative of their composition at the point can be expressed as the application of the derivative of the second function to the derivative of the first function at that point.

explanatories.PartialEquiv.left_inv: The left inverse property of a partial equivalence asserts that applying the inverse mapping to an element that has been mapped by the forward function returns the original element, provided the element is within the source set.

explanatories.VectorBundleCore.coordChange_comp: The theorem establishes that the composition of coordinate changes between different trivializations of a vector bundle at a common point yields the same result as a direct coordinate change between the first and the last trivializations.

explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.continuousOn: This theorem demonstrates that the function associated with a partial homeomorphism is continuous on its designated source set.

tangentCoordChange.comment:
In a manifold `M`, given two preferred charts indexed by `x y : M`, `tangentCoordChange I x y`
is the family of derivatives of the corresponding change-of-coordinates map. It takes junk values
outside the intersection of the sources of the two charts.

Note that this definition takes advantage of the fact that `tangentBundleCore` has the same base
sets as the preferred charts of the base manifold.

tangentBundleCore.isSmooth.fullDefinition: instance tangentBundleCore.isSmooth : (tangentBundleCore I M).IsSmooth I := by   refine ⟨fun i j => ?_⟩   rw [SmoothOn, contMDiffOn_iff_source_of_mem_maximalAtlas (subset_maximalAtlas I i.2),     contMDiffOn_iff_contDiffOn]   · refine ((contDiffOn_fderiv_coord_change I i j).congr fun x hx => ?_).mono ?_     · rw [PartialEquiv.trans_source'] at hx       simp_rw [Function.comp_apply, tangentBundleCore_coordChange, (i.1.extend I).right_inv hx.1]     · exact (i.1.extend_image_source_inter j.1 I).subset   · apply inter_subset_left

inTangentCoordinates.comment:
When `ϕ x` is a continuous linear map that changes vectors in charts around `f x` to vectors
in charts around `g x`, `inTangentCoordinates I I' f g ϕ x₀ x` is a coordinate change of
this continuous linear map that makes sense from charts around `f x₀` to charts around `g x₀`
by composing it with appropriate coordinate changes.
Note that the type of `ϕ` is more accurately
`Π x : N, TangentSpace I (f x) →L[𝕜] TangentSpace I' (g x)`.
We are unfolding `TangentSpace` in this type so that Lean recognizes that the type of `ϕ` doesn't
actually depend on `f` or `g`.

This is the underlying function of the trivializations of the hom of (pullbacks of) tangent spaces.

  {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {E' : Type u_3} [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E']
  {H : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H) {H' : Type u_5} [TopologicalSpace H']
  (I' : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E' H') {M : Type u_6} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M]
  {M' : Type u_7} [TopologicalSpace M'] [ChartedSpace H' M'] [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I' M'] {N : Type u_9}
  (f : N → M) (g : N → M') (ϕ : N → E →L[𝕜] E') {x₀ x : N} (hx : f x ∈ (chartAt H (f x₀)).source)
  (hy : g x ∈ (chartAt H' (g x₀)).source) :
  inTangentCoordinates I I' f g ϕ x₀ x =
    ((tangentBundleCore I' M').coordChange (achart H' (g x)) (achart H' (g x₀)) (g x)).comp
      ((ϕ x).comp ((tangentBundleCore I M).coordChange (achart H (f x₀)) (achart H (f x)) (f x)))

For a smooth vector bundle `E` over a manifold `B` and a smooth map `f : B' → B`, the pullback
vector bundle `f *ᵖ E` is a smooth vector bundle.

explanatories.smoothOn_coordChangeL: The smoothness of the coordinate change function between two trivializations of a smooth vector bundle is guaranteed on the intersection of their respective base sets.
explanatories.SmoothOn.comp: This theorem states that if two functions are smooth over their respective domains and the range of the first function is contained within the domain of the second function, then their composition is also smooth over the domain of the first function.
explanatories.ContMDiffMap.smooth: This theorem asserts that every continuously differentiable map is also classified as a smooth map between the respective manifolds.
explanatories.Smooth.smoothOn: The theorem states that if a function is smooth across its entire domain, then it is also smooth when restricted to any specific subset of that domain.
explanatories.ContMDiffOn.congr: This theorem states that if two functions agree on a set and one is continuously differentiable on that set, then the other function is also continuously differentiable on the same set.
explanatories.Trivialization.baseSet: The base set of a trivialization is defined as a subset of the base space associated with a given projection.
explanatories.Trivialization.pullback: A fiber bundle trivialization can be adapted to correspond to a trivialization on the pullback bundle via a continuous map from a base space.
explanatories.Trivialization.coordChangeL: This defines a continuous linear equivalence that represents the change of coordinates between two trivializations, which coincides with the identity when the given point is not in the base set of both trivializations.
explanatories.Trivialization.coordChangeL_apply: The theorem states that the change of coordinates between two linear trivializations at a point in their intersection of base sets maps a vector in the model space to the corresponding coordinate transformation defined by the second trivialization.
explanatories.Trivialization.coordChangeL_apply': This theorem provides an explicit formula for the application of a coordinate change between two linear trivializations, expressing it in terms of the components of the fibers mapped through the trivializations.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.

SmoothVectorBundle.pullback.fullDefinition: instance SmoothVectorBundle.pullback : SmoothVectorBundle F (f *ᵖ E) IB' where   smoothOn_coordChangeL := by     rintro _ _ ⟨e, he, rfl⟩ ⟨e', he', rfl⟩     refine ((smoothOn_coordChangeL _ e e').comp f.smooth.smoothOn fun b hb => hb).congr ?_     rintro b (hb : f b ∈ e.baseSet ∩ e'.baseSet); ext v     show ((e.pullback f).coordChangeL 𝕜 (e'.pullback f) b) v = (e.coordChangeL 𝕜 e' (f b)) v     rw [e.coordChangeL_apply e' hb, (e.pullback f).coordChangeL_apply' _]     exacts [rfl, hb]
SmoothVectorBundle.pullback.description: The definition states that the pullback of a smooth vector bundle via a smooth map results in another smooth vector bundle over the target manifold.

explanatories.Trivialization.baseSet: The base set of a trivialization is defined as a subset of the base space associated with a given projection.
explanatories.Trivialization.pullback: A fiber bundle trivialization can be adapted to correspond to a trivialization on the pullback bundle via a continuous map from a base space.
explanatories.Trivialization.coordChangeL: This defines a continuous linear equivalence that represents the change of coordinates between two trivializations, which coincides with the identity when the given point is not in the base set of both trivializations.
explanatories.Trivialization.coordChangeL_apply: The theorem states that the change of coordinates between two linear trivializations at a point in their intersection of base sets maps a vector in the model space to the corresponding coordinate transformation defined by the second trivialization.
explanatories.Trivialization.coordChangeL_apply': This theorem provides an explicit formula for the application of a coordinate change between two linear trivializations, expressing it in terms of the components of the fibers mapped through the trivializations.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.

smooth_vector_bundle.pullback.fullDefinition: instance SmoothVectorBundle.pullback : SmoothVectorBundle F (f *ᵖ E) IB' where   smoothOn_coordChangeL := by     rintro _ _ ⟨e, he, rfl⟩ ⟨e', he', rfl⟩     refine ((smoothOn_coordChangeL _ e e').comp f.smooth.smoothOn fun b hb => hb).congr ?_     rintro b (hb : f b ∈ e.baseSet ∩ e'.baseSet); ext v     show ((e.pullback f).coordChangeL 𝕜 (e'.pullback f) b) v = (e.coordChangeL 𝕜 e' (f b)) v     rw [e.coordChangeL_apply e' hb, (e.pullback f).coordChangeL_apply' _]     exacts [rfl, hb]
smooth_vector_bundle.pullback.description: The definition states that the pullback of a smooth vector bundle via a smooth map results in another smooth vector bundle over the target manifold.

explanatories.FiberBundle.mem_baseSet_trivializationAt: Every point in the base space is included in the base set of the corresponding local trivialization for the given fiber bundle.
explanatories.Trivialization.linear: This theorem establishes that the mapping defined by a trivialization at a point in its base set is a linear map with respect to a specified semiring.
explanatories.ContMDiffAt.neg: If a function is continuously differentiable at a point on a manifold, then its inverse is also continuously differentiable at that same point on the manifold.
explanatories.IsLinearMap.map_neg: This theorem asserts that a linear map preserves negation, meaning the image of the negation of an element is the negation of the image of that element.

cont_mdiff_section.has_neg.fullDefinition: instance instNeg : Neg Cₛ^n⟮I; F, V⟯ := by   refine ⟨fun s => ⟨-s, ?_⟩⟩   intro x₀   have hs := s.contMDiff x₀   rw [contMDiffAt_section] at hs ⊢   set e := trivializationAt F V x₀   refine hs.neg.congr_of_eventuallyEq ?_   refine eventually_of_mem (e.open_baseSet.mem_nhds <| mem_baseSet_trivializationAt F V x₀) ?_   intro x hx   apply (e.linear 𝕜 hx).map_neg

point, when read in the model vector space. This property will be lifted to manifolds to define
differentiable functions between manifolds.

MDifferentiableWithinAt.comment:
`MDifferentiableWithinAt I I' f s x` indicates that the function `f` between manifolds
has a derivative at the point `x` within the set `s`.
This is a generalization of `DifferentiableWithinAt` to manifolds.

We require continuity in the definition, as otherwise points close to `x` in `s` could be sent by
`f` outside of the chart domain around `f x`. Then the chart could do anything to the image points,
and in particular by coincidence `writtenInExtChartAt I I' x f` could be differentiable, while
this would not mean anything relevant.

HasMFDerivWithinAt.code:
HasMFDerivWithinAt.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H)
  {M : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] {E' : Type u_5} [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E']
  {H' : Type u_6} [TopologicalSpace H'] (I' : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E' H') {M' : Type u_7} [TopologicalSpace M']
  [ChartedSpace H' M'] [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M] [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I' M'] (f : M → M') (s : Set M)
  (x : M) (f' : TangentSpace I x →L[𝕜] TangentSpace I' (f x)) : Prop
HasMFDerivWithinAt.comment:
`HasMFDerivWithinAt I I' f s x f'` indicates that the function `f` between manifolds
has, at the point `x` and within the set `s`, the derivative `f'`. Here, `f'` is a continuous linear
map from the tangent space at `x` to the tangent space at `f x`.

This is a generalization of `HasFDerivWithinAt` to manifolds (as indicated by the prefix `m`).
The order of arguments is changed as the type of the derivative `f'` depends on the choice of `x`.

We require continuity in the definition, as otherwise points close to `x` in `s` could be sent by
`f` outside of the chart domain around `f x`. Then the chart could do anything to the image points,
and in particular by coincidence `writtenInExtChartAt I I' x f` could be differentiable, while
this would not mean anything relevant.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.ModelWithCorners.symm: This definition describes the inverse function of a model with corners, which is categorized as a partial equivalence between two types of spaces.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.symm: This definition describes the inverse of a partial homeomorphism, which relates two topological spaces in the opposite direction.
explanatories.PartialEquiv.symm: This defines the inverse of a partial equivalence, allowing for a corresponding mapping from one type back to another.
explanatories.ContinuousWithinAt: This defines the concept of a function being continuous at a point within a subset of a topological space, focusing on the behavior of the function as points approach that point while remaining within the subset.
explanatories.TangentSpace: The definition specifies the tangent space at a point on a smooth manifold as being equivalent to the corresponding vector space.
explanatories.HasFDerivWithinAt: A function has a specified continuous linear derivative at a point within a set if its behavior around that point can be approximated by the linear map in the limit as the input approaches the point from within the set.

HasMFDerivWithinAt.fullDefinition: def HasMFDerivWithinAt (f : M → M') (s : Set M) (x : M)     (f' : TangentSpace I x →L[𝕜] TangentSpace I' (f x)) :=   ContinuousWithinAt f s x ∧     HasFDerivWithinAt (writtenInExtChartAt I I' x f : E → E') f'       ((extChartAt I x).symm ⁻¹' s ∩ range I) ((extChartAt I x) x)
HasMFDerivWithinAt.description: This definition specifies the condition under which a function between manifolds has a derivative at a point within a set, characterized by a continuous linear map from the tangent space at that point to the tangent space at its image.

  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H}
  {M : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] {E' : Type u_5} [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E']
  {H' : Type u_6} [TopologicalSpace H'] {I' : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E' H'} {M' : Type u_7} [TopologicalSpace M']
  [ChartedSpace H' M'] {f f₁ : M → M'} {s : Set M} [Is : SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M]
  [I's : SmoothManifoldWithCorners I' M'] (h : ∀ x ∈ s, f x = f₁ x) (p : TangentBundle I M) (hp : p.proj ∈ s)
  (hs : UniqueMDiffWithinAt I s p.proj) : tangentMapWithin I I' f s p = tangentMapWithin I I' f₁ s p

explanatories.TangentBundle: The definition describes the tangent bundle of a smooth manifold as a type that represents its total space in a structured manner suitable for topology, linking the manifold with a model vector space.

tangent_map_within_congr.description: This theorem states that if two functions agree on a set and a point is uniquely differentiable within that set, then their tangent maps at that point are equivalent when viewed within the tangent spaces of their respective smooth manifolds.

mfderiv_prod_eq_add.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7, u_8, u_9, u_10} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
  {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace H]
  (I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H) {M : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M]
  {E' : Type u_5} [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E'] {H' : Type u_6} [TopologicalSpace H']
  (I' : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E' H') {M' : Type u_7} [TopologicalSpace M'] [ChartedSpace H' M']
  [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I' M'] {E'' : Type u_8} [NormedAddCommGroup E''] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E''] {H'' : Type u_9}
  [TopologicalSpace H''] (I'' : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E'' H'') {M'' : Type u_10} [TopologicalSpace M'']
  [ChartedSpace H'' M''] [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I'' M''] {f : M × M' → M''} {p : M × M'}
  (hf : MDifferentiableAt (I.prod I') I'' f p) :
  mfderiv (I.prod I') I'' f p =
    let_fun this :=
      mfderiv (I.prod I') I'' (fun z => f (z.1, p.2)) p + mfderiv (I.prod I') I'' (fun z => f (p.1, z.2)) p;
    this

  [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H} {M : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace H M] [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M] {E' : Type u_5} [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E'] {z : M}
  {f g : M → E'} (hf : MDifferentiableAt I 𝓘(𝕜, E') f z) (hg : MDifferentiableAt I 𝓘(𝕜, E') g z) :
  mfderiv I 𝓘(𝕜, E') (f - g) z = mfderiv I 𝓘(𝕜, E') f z - mfderiv I 𝓘(𝕜, E') g z

its derivative has dense range, then `f '' s` has the unique differential property at `f x`.

explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.MDifferentiable: This definition indicates whether a partial homeomorphism between manifolds qualifies as a local diffeomorphism at points in its source space.
explanatories.Trivialization.toPartialHomeomorph: A trivialization establishes a structure that creates a partial homeomorphism between a given space and the product of its base space with its fiber.
explanatories.ModelWithCorners.prod: This definition specifies how to create a new model with corners on the product of two spaces from existing models with corners on each of those spaces.
explanatories.UniqueMDiffWithinAt.prod: This theorem states that if two points are uniquely differentiable within their respective sets, then their product at those points is also uniquely differentiable within the product of the two sets at the combined point.

Trivialization.mdifferentiable.description: This theorem establishes that if a structure is given a trivialization, then the induced mapping between the corresponding product structures is differentiable in a way that maintains the manifold's local properties.

Diffeomorph.toTransDiffeomorph.fullDefinition: def toTransDiffeomorph (e : E ≃ₘ[𝕜] F) : M ≃ₘ⟮I, I.transDiffeomorph e⟯ M where   toEquiv := Equiv.refl M   contMDiff_toFun x := by     refine contMDiffWithinAt_iff'.2 ⟨continuousWithinAt_id, ?_⟩     refine e.contDiff.contDiffWithinAt.congr' (fun y hy ↦ ?_) ?_     · simp only [Equiv.coe_refl, id, (· ∘ ·), I.coe_extChartAt_transDiffeomorph,         (extChartAt I x).right_inv hy.1]     · exact       ⟨(extChartAt I x).map_source (mem_extChartAt_source I x), trivial, by simp only [mfld_simps]⟩   contMDiff_invFun x := by     refine contMDiffWithinAt_iff'.2 ⟨continuousWithinAt_id, ?_⟩     refine e.symm.contDiff.contDiffWithinAt.congr' (fun y hy => ?_) ?_     · simp only [mem_inter_iff, I.extChartAt_transDiffeomorph_target] at hy       simp only [Equiv.coe_refl, Equiv.refl_symm, id, (· ∘ ·),         I.coe_extChartAt_transDiffeomorph_symm, (extChartAt I x).right_inv hy.1]     exact ⟨(extChartAt _ x).map_source (mem_extChartAt_source _ x), trivial, by       simp only [e.symm_apply_apply, Equiv.refl_symm, Equiv.coe_refl, mfld_simps]⟩

explanatories.ModelWithCorners.coe_extChartAt_transDif: This theorem establishes a relationship between the charts of a model with corners and a diffeomorphism by showing how the chart at a point transforms under the composition of the diffeomorphism and the chart.

ContMDiffAt.mfderiv.code:
ContMDiffAt.mfderiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7, u_8, u_9, u_10} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
  {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace H]
  {I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H} {M : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]
  [Is : SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M] {E' : Type u_5} [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E'] {H' : Type u_6}
  [TopologicalSpace H'] {I' : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E' H'} {M' : Type u_7} [TopologicalSpace M'] [ChartedSpace H' M']
  [I's : SmoothManifoldWithCorners I' M'] {F : Type u_8} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] {G : Type u_9}
  [TopologicalSpace G] {J : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 F G} {N : Type u_10} [TopologicalSpace N] [ChartedSpace G N]
  [Js : SmoothManifoldWithCorners J N] {m n : ℕ∞} {x₀ : N} (f : N → M → M') (g : N → M)
  (hf : ContMDiffAt (J.prod I) I' n (uncurry f) (x₀, g x₀)) (hg : ContMDiffAt J I m g x₀) (hmn : m + 1 ≤ n) :
  ContMDiffAt J 𝓘(𝕜, E →L[𝕜] E') m
    (inTangentCoordinates I I' g (fun x => f x (g x)) (fun x => mfderiv I I' (f x) (g x)) x₀) x₀
ContMDiffAt.mfderiv.comment:
The function that sends `x` to the `y`-derivative of `f(x,y)` at `g(x)` is `C^m` at `x₀`,
where the derivative is taken as a continuous linear map.
We have to assume that `f` is `C^n` at `(x₀, g(x₀))` for `n ≥ m + 1` and `g` is `C^m` at `x₀`.
We have to insert a coordinate change from `x₀` to `x` to make the derivative sensible.
This result is used to show that maps into the 1-jet bundle and cotangent bundle are smooth.
`ContMDiffAt.mfderiv_const` is a special case of this.

This result should be generalized to a `ContMDiffWithinAt` for `mfderivWithin`.
If we do that, we can deduce `ContMDiffOn.contMDiffOn_tangentMapWithin` from this.

TangentBundle.tangentMap_tangentBundle_pure.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
  {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace H]
  (I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H) (M : Type u_4) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]
  [Is : SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M] (p : TangentBundle I M) :
  tangentMap I I.tangent (zeroSection E (TangentSpace I)) p =
    { proj := { proj := p.proj, snd := 0 }, snd := (p.snd, 0) }
TangentBundle.tangentMap_tangentBundle_p.comment:
The derivative of the zero section of the tangent bundle maps `⟨x, v⟩` to `⟨⟨x, 0⟩, ⟨v, 0⟩⟩`.

Note that, as currently framed, this is a statement in coordinates, thus reliant on the choice
of the coordinate system we use on the tangent bundle.

However, the result itself is coordinate-dependent only to the extent that the coordinates
determine a splitting of the tangent bundle.  Moreover, there is a canonical splitting at each
point of the zero section (since there is a canonical horizontal space there, the tangent space
to the zero section, in addition to the canonical vertical space which is the kernel of the
derivative of the projection), and this canonical splitting is also the one that comes from the
coordinates on the tangent bundle in our definitions. So this statement is not as crazy as it
may seem.

  (I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H) (M : Type u_4) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]

tangent_bundle.tangent_map_tangent_bundl.comment:
The derivative of the zero section of the tangent bundle maps `⟨x, v⟩` to `⟨⟨x, 0⟩, ⟨v, 0⟩⟩`.

Note that, as currently framed, this is a statement in coordinates, thus reliant on the choice
of the coordinate system we use on the tangent bundle.

However, the result itself is coordinate-dependent only to the extent that the coordinates
determine a splitting of the tangent bundle.  Moreover, there is a canonical splitting at each
point of the zero section (since there is a canonical horizontal space there, the tangent space
to the zero section, in addition to the canonical vertical space which is the kernel of the
derivative of the projection), and this canonical splitting is also the one that comes from the
coordinates on the tangent bundle in our definitions. So this statement is not as crazy as it
may seem.

TODO define splittings of vector bundles; state this result invariantly.

  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {H : Type uH} [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} {M : Type uM}
  [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] {c : M} (f : SmoothBumpFunction I c) {s : Set M} (hsc : IsClosed s)
  (hs : s ⊆ support ↑f) :
  ∃ r ∈ Ioo 0 f.rOut, s ⊆ (chartAt H c).source ∩ ↑(extChartAt I c) ⁻¹' ball (↑(extChartAt I c) c) r
SmoothBumpFunction.exists_r_pos_lt_subse.comment:
If `f` is a smooth bump function and `s` closed subset of the support of `f` (i.e., of the open
ball of radius `f.rOut`), then there exists `0 < r < f.rOut` such that `s` is a subset of the open
ball of radius `r`. Formally, `s ⊆ e.source ∩ e ⁻¹' (ball (e c) r)`, where `e = extChartAt I c`.

IsIntegralCurve.comment:
If `v : M → TM` is a vector field on `M`, `IsIntegralCurve γ v` means `γ : ℝ → M` is a global
integral curve of `v`. That is, `γ t` is tangent to `v (γ t)` for all `t : ℝ`.

explanatories.TangentSpace: The definition specifies the tangent space at a point on a smooth manifold as being equivalent to the corresponding vector space.
explanatories.HasMFDerivAt: This definition specifies that a function between manifolds has a derivative at a specific point if it is represented by a continuous linear map from the tangent space at that point to the tangent space at the image of the point.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight: The construction defines a continuous linear map that takes a scalar-valued linear map and an element from a module, producing a new linear map by scaling the output by the given element.

IsIntegralCurve.fullDefinition: def IsIntegralCurve (γ : ℝ → M) (v : (x : M) → TangentSpace I x) : Prop :=   ∀ t : ℝ, HasMFDerivAt 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) I γ t ((1 : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ).smulRight (v (γ t)))
IsIntegralCurve.description: This definition states that a curve is considered an integral curve of a given vector field if it remains tangent to the field at every point along the curve for all real numbers.

IsIntegralCurveOn.comment:
If `γ : ℝ → M` is $C^1$ on `s : Set ℝ` and `v` is a vector field on `M`,
`IsIntegralCurveOn γ v s` means `γ t` is tangent to `v (γ t)` for all `t ∈ s`. The value of `γ`
outside of `s` is irrelevant and considered junk.

explanatories.LocallyFinite: A family of sets in a topological space is locally finite if each point in the space has a neighborhood that intersects only finitely many sets from the family.
explanatories.Function.support: This definition introduces the support of a function as the set of inputs for which the function does not map to the additive identity.
explanatories.PartitionOfUnity.locallyFinite': This theorem demonstrates that a partition of unity associated with a given family of sets in a topological space is locally finite, meaning that each point in the space has a neighborhood that intersects only finitely many of these sets.
explanatories.PartitionOfUnity.nonneg': This theorem establishes that the continuous functions derived from a partition of unity are non-negative everywhere in the specified topological space.
explanatories.PartitionOfUnity.sum_eq_one': This theorem asserts that for any point included in the underlying set of a partition of unity in a topological space, the sum of the values of the associated functions at that point equals one.
explanatories.PartitionOfUnity.sum_le_one': This theorem states that the sum of the function values obtained from a partition of unity at any point in the topological space is less than or equal to one.
explanatories.Smooth.add: Theorem states that if two functions are smooth according to a given model with corners, then their product is also smooth within the same model.

SmoothPartitionOfUnity.toFun.fullDefinition: toFun : ι → C^∞⟮I, M; 𝓘(ℝ), ℝ⟯   /-- Around each point, there are only finitely many nonzero functions in the family. -/   locallyFinite' : LocallyFinite fun i => support (toFun i)   /-- All the functions in the partition of unity are nonnegative. -/   nonneg' : ∀ i x, 0 ≤ toFun i x   /-- The functions in the partition of unity add up to `1` at any point of `s`. -/   sum_eq_one' : ∀ x ∈ s, ∑ᶠ i, toFun i x = 1   /-- The functions in the partition of unity add up to at most `1` everywhere. -/   sum_le_one' : ∀ x, ∑ᶠ i, toFun i x ≤ 1

smooth_partition_of_unity.is_subordinate.comment:
If `f` is a smooth partition of unity on a set `s : Set M` subordinate to a family of open sets
`U : ι → Set M` and `g : ι → M → F` is a family of functions such that `g i` is $C^n$ smooth on
`U i`, then the sum `fun x ↦ ∑ᶠ i, f i x • g i x` is $C^n$ smooth on the whole manifold.

BumpCovering.toSmoothPartitionOfUnity.comment:
A `BumpCovering` such that all functions in this covering are smooth generates a smooth
partition of unity.

In our formalization, not every `f : BumpCovering ι M s` with smooth functions `f i` is a
`SmoothBumpCovering`; instead, a `SmoothBumpCovering` is a covering by supports of
`SmoothBumpFunction`s. So, we define `BumpCovering.toSmoothPartitionOfUnity`, then reuse it
in `SmoothBumpCovering.toSmoothPartitionOfUnity`.

explanatories.BumpCovering.smooth_toPartitionOfUnity: This theorem demonstrates that if a bump covering consists of smooth functions, then the corresponding function from the partition of unity derived from this covering is also smooth.
explanatories.BumpCovering.IsSubordinate.toPartitionOf: This theorem shows that if a bump covering is subordinate to a collection of sets, then its associated partition of unity is also subordinate to the same collection of sets.

  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {H : Type uH} [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) {M : Type uM}
  [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] {s : Set M} {U : M → Set M} [T2Space M] [SigmaCompactSpace M]
  (hs : IsClosed s) (hU : ∀ x ∈ s, U x ∈ 𝓝 x) : ∃ ι f, f.IsSubordinate U
SmoothBumpCovering.exists_isSubordinate.comment:
Let `M` be a smooth manifold with corners modelled on a finite dimensional real vector space.
Suppose also that `M` is a Hausdorff `σ`-compact topological space. Let `s` be a closed set
in `M` and `U : M → Set M` be a collection of sets such that `U x ∈ 𝓝 x` for every `x ∈ s`.
Then there exists a smooth bump covering of `s` that is subordinate to `U`.

SmoothBumpCovering.toSmoothPartitionOfUnity_eq_mul_prod.{uι, uE, uH, uM} {ι : Type uι} {E : Type uE}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {H : Type uH} [TopologicalSpace H]

exists_smooth_zero_one_of_isClosed.code:
exists_smooth_zero_one_of_isClosed.{uE, uH, uM} {E : Type uE} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {H : Type uH} [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) {M : Type uM}
  [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M] [T2Space M] [SigmaCompactSpace M]
  {s t : Set M} (hs : IsClosed s) (ht : IsClosed t) (hd : Disjoint s t) :
  ∃ f, EqOn (⇑f) 0 s ∧ EqOn (⇑f) 1 t ∧ ∀ (x : M), f x ∈ Icc 0 1
exists_smooth_zero_one_of_isClosed.comment:
Given two disjoint closed sets `s, t` in a Hausdorff σ-compact finite dimensional manifold,
there exists an infinitely smooth function that is equal to `0` on `s` and to `1` on `t`.
See also `exists_msmooth_zero_iff_one_iff_of_isClosed`, which ensures additionally that
`f` is equal to `0` exactly on `s` and to `1` exactly on `t`.

explanatories.BumpCovering.coe_single: This theorem establishes that the function associated with a single-element bump covering corresponds to the constant function equal to one at that specific index in the given topological space.

exists_contMDiffOn_forall_mem_convex_of_local.{uE, uH, uM, uF} {E : Type uE} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {F : Type uF} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] {H : Type uH} [TopologicalSpace H]
  (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) {M : Type uM} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M]
  [SigmaCompactSpace M] [T2Space M] {t : M → Set F} {n : ℕ∞} (ht : ∀ (x : M), Convex ℝ (t x))
  (Hloc : ∀ (x : M), ∃ U ∈ 𝓝 x, ∃ g, ContMDiffOn I 𝓘(ℝ, F) n g U ∧ ∀ y ∈ U, g y ∈ t y) : ∃ g, ∀ (x : M), g x ∈ t x
exists_contMDiffOn_forall_mem_convex_of_.comment:
Let `M` be a σ-compact Hausdorff finite dimensional topological manifold. Let `t : M → Set F`
be a family of convex sets. Suppose that for each point `x : M` there exists a neighborhood
`U ∈ 𝓝 x` and a function `g : M → F` such that `g` is $C^n$ smooth on `U` and `g y ∈ t y` for all
`y ∈ U`. Then there exists a $C^n$ smooth function `g : C^∞⟮I, M; 𝓘(ℝ, F), F⟯` such that `g x ∈ t x`
for all `x`. See also `exists_smooth_forall_mem_convex_of_local` and
`exists_smooth_forall_mem_convex_of_local_const`.

explanatories.ContMDiffOn: The definition characterizes a function as being continuously differentiable up to a specified order within a set of a manifold if it is continuous and maintains that differentiability across all charts around its points.

exists_contMDiffOn_forall_mem_convex_of_.description: This theorem establishes the existence of a smooth function that stays within a family of convex sets defined locally around each point in a manifold, based on local conditions of smoothness and containment.

exists_smooth_forall_mem_convex_of_local.comment:
Let `M` be a σ-compact Hausdorff finite dimensional topological manifold. Let `t : M → Set F`

Then there exists a smooth function `g : C^∞⟮I, M; 𝓘(ℝ, F), F⟯` such that `g x ∈ t x` for all `x`.

Let `M` be a σ-compact Hausdorff finite dimensional topological manifold. Let `t : M → Set F` be
a family of convex sets. Suppose that for each point `x : M` there exists a vector `c : F` such that
for all `y` in a neighborhood of `x` we have `c ∈ t y`. Then there exists a smooth function

Emetric.exists_smooth_forall_closedBall_subset.{uι, uE, uH, u_1} {ι : Type uι} {E : Type uE} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {H : Type uH} [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H)
  {M : Type u_1} [EMetricSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M] [SigmaCompactSpace M]
  {K U : ι → Set M} (hK : ∀ (i : ι), IsClosed (K i)) (hU : ∀ (i : ι), IsOpen (U i)) (hKU : ∀ (i : ι), K i ⊆ U i)
  (hfin : LocallyFinite K) :
  ∃ δ, (∀ (x : M), 0 < δ x) ∧ ∀ (i : ι), ∀ x ∈ K i, EMetric.closedBall x (ENNReal.ofReal (δ x)) ⊆ U i
Emetric.exists_smooth_forall_closedBall_.comment:
Let `M` be a smooth σ-compact manifold with extended distance. Let `K : ι → Set M` be a locally
finite family of closed sets, let `U : ι → Set M` be a family of open sets such that `K i ⊆ U i` for
all `i`. Then there exists a positive smooth function `δ : M → ℝ≥0` such that for any `i` and
`x ∈ K i`, we have `EMetric.closedBall x (δ x) ⊆ U i`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.LocallyFinite: A family of sets in a topological space is locally finite if each point in the space has a neighborhood that intersects only finitely many sets from the family.
explanatories.EMetric.closedBall: The closed ball around a point in a pseudo-metric space consists of all points whose distance from that point is less than or equal to a specified non-negative extended real number.
explanatories.ENNReal.ofReal: This definition describes a function that converts a real number into the extended nonnegative real numbers, returning the number itself if it is nonnegative and zero if it is negative.
explanatories.Metric.closedBall: The closed ball around a point in a pseudo-metric space consists of all points whose distance from that point is less than or equal to a specified radius.

Emetric.exists_smooth_forall_closedBall_.description: This theorem establishes the existence of a positive smooth function such that for any point in a locally finite family of closed sets within a smooth manifold, closed balls centered at those points are contained within corresponding open sets.

  (hfin : LocallyFinite K) :

emetric.exists_smooth_forall_closed_ball.comment:
Let `M` be a smooth σ-compact manifold with extended distance. Let `K : ι → Set M` be a locally
finite family of closed sets, let `U : ι → Set M` be a family of open sets such that `K i ⊆ U i` for
all `i`. Then there exists a positive smooth function `δ : M → ℝ≥0` such that for any `i` and
`x ∈ K i`, we have `EMetric.closedBall x (δ x) ⊆ U i`.

explanatories.contMDiff_pi_space: This theorem states that a function is continuously differentiable on a manifold if and only if each of its component functions, which map to a product of spaces, is continuously differentiable individually.
explanatories.SmoothBumpFunction.smooth_smul: This theorem states that the product of a smooth bump function and another smooth function is smooth on the entire manifold if the latter is smooth within the chart's source.
explanatories.contMDiffOn_extChartAt: This theorem asserts that the external chart at a point of a manifold is continuously differentiable to a specified order on the source set of its corresponding chart.
explanatories.Smooth.prod_mk_space: This theorem asserts that if two functions are smooth, then their product function, which maps into the Cartesian product of their respective target spaces, is also smooth.
explanatories.SmoothBumpFunction.smooth: This theorem asserts that a smooth bump function is infinitely differentiable, meaning it is smooth with respect to a given smooth structure.
explanatories.ContMDiffMap.smooth: This theorem asserts that every continuously differentiable map is also classified as a smooth map between the respective manifolds.
explanatories.Diffeomorph.smooth: This theorem asserts that a diffeomorphism between two manifolds preserves smoothness under the specified differentiable structures.

  [NormedSpace ℂ E] {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F] {H : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace H]

  (hc : IsLocalMax (norm ∘ f) c) : ∀ᶠ (y : M) in 𝓝 c, ‖f y‖ = ‖f c‖
Complex.norm_eventually_eq_of_mdifferent.comment:
**Maximum modulus principle**: if `f : M → F` is complex differentiable in a neighborhood of `c`
and the norm `‖f z‖` has a local maximum at `c`, then `‖f z‖` is locally constant in a neighborhood
of `c`. This is a manifold version of `Complex.norm_eventually_eq_of_isLocalMax`.

explanatories.MDifferentiableAt: This definition specifies the condition under which a function between manifolds is considered to have a derivative at a particular point, emphasizing the importance of continuity around that point to ensure meaningful differentiation within the appropriate chart domains.
explanatories.IsLocalMax: This definition indicates that a function reaches a local maximum at a point if, in some neighborhood of that point, its value is greater than or equal to the function values at all other points nearby.
explanatories.ContinuousOn.norm: If a function is continuous on a set, then the function that assigns the norm to each point in that set is also continuous on the same set.

Complex.norm_eventually_eq_of_mdifferent.description: This theorem asserts that if a complex-valued function has a local maximum of its norm at a point and is differentiable in a neighborhood of that point, then the norm remains constant in that neighborhood.

MDifferentiableOn.norm_eqOn_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℂ E] {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F] {H : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace H]
  {I : ModelWithCorners ℂ E H} [I.Boundaryless] {M : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]
  [SmoothManifoldWithCorners I M] {f : M → F} {U : Set M} {c : M} (hd : MDifferentiableOn I 𝓘(ℂ, F) f U)
  (hc : IsPreconnected U) (ho : IsOpen U) (hcU : c ∈ U) (hm : IsMaxOn (norm ∘ f) U c) :
  EqOn (norm ∘ f) (const M ‖f c‖) U
MDifferentiableOn.norm_eqOn_of_isPreconn.comment:
**Maximum modulus principle** on a connected set. Let `U` be a (pre)connected open set in a
complex normed space. Let `f : E → F` be a function that is complex differentiable on `U`. Suppose
that `‖f x‖` takes its maximum value on `U` at `c ∈ U`. Then `‖f x‖ = ‖f c‖` for all `x ∈ U`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.IsPreconnected: This definition describes a preconnected set as one that cannot be divided into two or more non-empty disjoint open sets.
explanatories.IsMaxOn: A property indicating that a function achieves a maximum value at a point within a specified set if its value at that point is greater than or equal to its value at any other point in that set, without requiring that the point belongs to the set.
explanatories.Set.EqOn: Two functions are considered equal on a specified set if they produce the same output for every input from that set.
explanatories.ContinuousOn.norm: If a function is continuous on a set, then the function that assigns the norm to each point in that set is also continuous on the same set.

MDifferentiableOn.norm_eqOn_of_isPreconn.description: This theorem states that if a complex-valued function is differentiable on a connected open set and achieves its maximum norm at a particular point within that set, then the norm is constant throughout the entire set.

AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.pushfo.fullDefinition: def pushforwardDiagramToColimit (F : J ⥤ PresheafedSpace.{_, _, v} C) :     J ⥤ (Presheaf C (colimit (F ⋙ PresheafedSpace.forget C)))ᵒᵖ where   obj j := op (colimit.ι (F ⋙ PresheafedSpace.forget C) j _* (F.obj j).presheaf)   map {j j'} f :=     ((pushforward C (colimit.ι (F ⋙ PresheafedSpace.forget C) j')).map (F.map f).c ≫       (Pushforward.comp  ((F ⋙ PresheafedSpace.forget C).map f)         (colimit.ι (F ⋙ PresheafedSpace.forget C) j') (F.obj j).presheaf).inv ≫       (pushforwardEq (colimit.w (F ⋙ PresheafedSpace.forget C) f) (F.obj j).presheaf).hom).op   map_id j := by     apply (opEquiv _ _).injective     refine NatTrans.ext _ _ (funext fun U => ?_)     induction U with     | h U =>       simp [opEquiv]       rfl   map_comp {j₁ j₂ j₃} f g := by     apply (opEquiv _ _).injective     refine NatTrans.ext _ _ (funext fun U => ?_)     dsimp [opEquiv]     have :       op ((Opens.map (F.map g).base).obj           ((Opens.map (colimit.ι (F ⋙ forget C) j₃)).obj U.unop)) =         op ((Opens.map (colimit.ι (F ⋙ PresheafedSpace.forget C) j₂)).obj (unop U)) := by       apply unop_injective       rw [← Opens.map_comp_obj]       congr       exact colimit.w (F ⋙ PresheafedSpace.forget C) g     simp only [map_comp_c_app, pushforward_obj_obj, pushforward_map_app, comp_base,       pushforwardEq_hom_app, op_obj, Opens.map_comp_obj, id_comp, assoc, eqToHom_map_comp,       NatTrans.naturality_assoc, pushforward_obj_map, eqToHom_unop]     simp [NatTrans.congr (α := (F.map f).c) this] set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.GlueData.f_invApp_f_app.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (D : GlueData C)
  (i j k : D.J) (U : Opens ↑↑(D.V (i, j))) :
  invApp (D.f i j) U ≫ (D.f i k).c.app (op ((opensFunctor (D.f i j)).obj U)) =
    (pullback.fst (D.f i j) (D.f i k)).c.app (op U) ≫
      invApp (pullback.snd (D.f i j) (D.f i k))
          (unop (op ((Opens.map (pullback.fst (D.f i j) (D.f i k)).base).toPrefunctor.1 (unop (op U))))) ≫
        (D.V (i, k)).presheaf.map (eqToHom ⋯)

AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.GlueData.snd_invApp_t_app'.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (D : GlueData C)
  (i j k : D.J) (U : Opens ↑↑(pullback (D.f i j) (D.f i k))) :
  ∃ (eq :
    (Opens.map (D.t k i).base).op.obj (op ((opensFunctor (pullback.snd (D.f i j) (D.f i k))).obj U)) =
      op
        ((opensFunctor (pullback.fst (D.f k i) (D.f k j))).obj
          (unop (op { carrier := ⇑(D.t' k i j).base ⁻¹' ↑(unop (op U)), is_open' := ⋯ })))),
    invApp (pullback.snd (D.f i j) (D.f i k)) U ≫
        (D.t k i).c.app (op ((opensFunctor (pullback.snd (D.f i j) (D.f i k))).obj U)) ≫
          (D.V (k, i)).presheaf.map (eqToHom eq) =
      (D.t' k i j).c.app (op U) ≫
        invApp (pullback.fst (D.f k i) (D.f k j))
          (unop (op { carrier := ⇑(D.t' k i j).base ⁻¹' ↑(unop (op U)), is_open' := ⋯ }))

AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.GlueData.f_invApp_f_app_assoc.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (D : GlueData C)
  (i j k : D.J) (U : Opens ↑↑(D.V (i, j))) {Z : C}
  (h :
    ((TopCat.Presheaf.pushforward C (D.f i k).base).obj (D.V (i, k)).presheaf).obj
        (op ((opensFunctor (D.f i j)).obj U)) ⟶
      Z) :
  invApp (D.f i j) U ≫ (D.f i k).c.app (op ((opensFunctor (D.f i j)).obj U)) ≫ h =
    (pullback.fst (D.f i j) (D.f i k)).c.app (op U) ≫
      invApp (pullback.snd (D.f i j) (D.f i k)) ((Opens.map (pullback.fst (D.f i j) (D.f i k)).base).toPrefunctor.1 U) ≫
        (D.V (i, k)).presheaf.map (eqToHom ⋯) ≫ h

AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.GlueData.opensImagePreimageMap_app'.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  (D : GlueData C) [HasLimits C] (i j k : D.J) (U : Opens ↑↑(D.U i)) :
  ∃ (eq :
    op
        ((opensFunctor (pullback.snd (D.f j i) (D.f j k))).obj
          (unop
            (op
              ((Opens.map (pullback.fst (D.f j i) (D.f j k) ≫ D.t j i ≫ D.f i j).base).toPrefunctor.1
                (unop (op U)))))) =
      (Opens.map (D.f j k).base).op.obj (op ((Opens.map (D.ι j).base).obj (⋯.functor.obj U)))),
    D.opensImagePreimageMap i j U ≫ (D.f j k).c.app (op ((Opens.map (D.ι j).base).obj (⋯.functor.obj U))) =
      (pullback.fst (D.f j i) (D.f j k) ≫ D.t j i ≫ D.f i j).c.app (op U) ≫
        invApp (pullback.snd (D.f j i) (D.f j k))
            (unop
              (op
                ((Opens.map (pullback.fst (D.f j i) (D.f j k) ≫ D.t j i ≫ D.f i j).base).toPrefunctor.1
                  (unop (op U))))) ≫
          (D.V (j, k)).presheaf.map (eqToHom eq)

AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.GlueData.opensImagePreimageMap_app_assoc.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  (D : GlueData C) [HasLimits C] (i j k : D.J) (U : Opens ↑↑(D.U i)) {X' : C}
  (f' :
    ((TopCat.Presheaf.pushforward C (D.f j k).base).obj (D.V (j, k)).presheaf).obj
        (op ((Opens.map (D.ι j).base).obj (⋯.functor.obj U))) ⟶
      X') :
  D.opensImagePreimageMap i j U ≫ (D.f j k).c.app (op ((Opens.map (D.ι j).base).obj (⋯.functor.obj U))) ≫ f' =
    (pullback.fst (D.f j i) (D.f j k) ≫ D.t j i ≫ D.f i j).c.app (op U) ≫
      invApp (pullback.snd (D.f j i) (D.f j k))
          (unop
            (op
              ((Opens.map (pullback.fst (D.f j i) (D.f j k) ≫ D.t j i ≫ D.f i j).base).toPrefunctor.1 (unop (op U))))) ≫
        (D.V (j, k)).presheaf.map (eqToHom ⋯) ≫ f'

AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.GlueDa.fullDefinition: def ιInvAppπApp {i : D.J} (U : Opens (D.U i).carrier) (j) :     (𝖣.U i).presheaf.obj (op U) ⟶ (D.diagramOverOpen U).obj (op j) := by   rcases j with (⟨j, k⟩ | j)   · refine       D.opensImagePreimageMap i j U ≫ (D.f j k).c.app _ ≫ (D.V (j, k)).presheaf.map (eqToHom ?_)     rw [Functor.op_obj]     congr 1; ext1     dsimp only [Functor.op_obj, Opens.map_coe, unop_op, IsOpenMap.functor_obj_coe]     rw [Set.preimage_preimage]     change (D.f j k ≫ 𝖣.ι j).base ⁻¹' _ = _     -- Porting note: used to be `congr 3`     refine congr_arg (· ⁻¹' _) ?_     convert congr_arg (ContinuousMap.toFun (α := D.V ⟨j, k⟩) (β := D.glued) ·) ?_     refine congr_arg (PresheafedSpace.Hom.base (C := C) ·) ?_     exact colimit.w 𝖣.diagram.multispan (WalkingMultispan.Hom.fst (j, k))   · exact D.opensImagePreimageMap i j U

AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.GlueData.snd_invApp_t_app_assoc.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  (D : GlueData C) (i j k : D.J) (U : Opens ↑↑(pullback (D.f i j) (D.f i k))) {Z : C}
  (h :
    ((TopCat.Presheaf.pushforward C (D.t k i).base).obj (D.V (k, i)).presheaf).obj
        (op ((opensFunctor (pullback.snd (D.f i j) (D.f i k))).obj U)) ⟶
      Z) :
  invApp (pullback.snd (D.f i j) (D.f i k)) U ≫
      (D.t k i).c.app (op ((opensFunctor (pullback.snd (D.f i j) (D.f i k))).obj U)) ≫ h =
    (D.t' k i j).c.app (op U) ≫
      invApp (pullback.fst (D.f k i) (D.f k j)) { carrier := ⇑(D.t' k i j).base ⁻¹' ↑U, is_open' := ⋯ } ≫
        (D.V (k, i)).presheaf.map (eqToHom ⋯) ≫ h

AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.GlueDa.fullDefinition: def ιInvApp {i : D.J} (U : Opens (D.U i).carrier) :     (D.U i).presheaf.obj (op U) ⟶ limit (D.diagramOverOpen U) :=   limit.lift (D.diagramOverOpen U)     { pt := (D.U i).presheaf.obj (op U)       π :=         { app := fun j => D.ιInvAppπApp U (unop j)           naturality := fun {X Y} f' => by             induction X using Opposite.rec' with | h X => ?_             induction Y using Opposite.rec' with | h Y => ?_             let f : Y ⟶ X := f'.unop; have : f' = f.op := rfl; clear_value f; subst this             rcases f with (_ | ⟨j, k⟩ | ⟨j, k⟩)             · erw [Category.id_comp, CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id]               rw [Category.comp_id]             · erw [Category.id_comp]; congr 1             erw [Category.id_comp]             -- It remains to show that the blue is equal to red + green in the original diagram.             -- The proof strategy is illustrated in ![this diagram](https://i.imgur.com/mBzV1Rx.png)             -- where we prove red = pink = light-blue = green = blue.             change               D.opensImagePreimageMap i j U ≫                   (D.f j k).c.app _ ≫ (D.V (j, k)).presheaf.map (eqToHom _) =                 D.opensImagePreimageMap _ _ _ ≫                   ((D.f k j).c.app _ ≫ (D.t j k).c.app _) ≫ (D.V (j, k)).presheaf.map (eqToHom _)             erw [opensImagePreimageMap_app_assoc]             simp_rw [Category.assoc]             erw [opensImagePreimageMap_app_assoc, (D.t j k).c.naturality_assoc]             rw [snd_invApp_t_app_assoc]             erw [← PresheafedSpace.comp_c_app_assoc]             -- light-blue = green is relatively easy since the part that differs does not involve             -- partial inverses.             have :               D.t' j k i ≫ (π₁ k, i, j) ≫ D.t k i ≫ 𝖣.f i k =                 (pullbackSymmetry _ _).hom ≫ (π₁ j, i, k) ≫ D.t j i ≫ D.f i j := by               rw [← 𝖣.t_fac_assoc, 𝖣.t'_comp_eq_pullbackSymmetry_assoc,                 pullbackSymmetry_hom_comp_snd_assoc, pullback.condition, 𝖣.t_fac_assoc]             rw [congr_app this]             erw [PresheafedSpace.comp_c_app_assoc (pullbackSymmetry _ _).hom]             simp_rw [Category.assoc]             congr 1             rw [← IsIso.eq_inv_comp]             erw [IsOpenImmersion.inv_invApp]             simp_rw [Category.assoc]             erw [NatTrans.naturality_assoc, ← PresheafedSpace.comp_c_app_assoc,               congr_app (pullbackSymmetry_hom_comp_snd _ _)]             simp_rw [Category.assoc]             erw [IsOpenImmersion.inv_naturality_assoc, IsOpenImmersion.inv_naturality_assoc,               IsOpenImmersion.inv_naturality_assoc, IsOpenImmersion.app_invApp_assoc]             repeat' erw [← (D.V (j, k)).presheaf.map_comp]             -- Porting note: was just `congr`             exact congr_arg ((D.V (j, k)).presheaf.map ·) rfl } }

AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.GlueDa.code:
AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.GlueData.ιInvApp_π.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (D : GlueData C)
  [HasLimits C] {i : D.J} (U : Opens ↑↑(D.U i)) :
  ∃ (eq :
    op U =
      op
        ((Opens.map (colimit.ι D.diagram.multispan (unop (op (WalkingMultispan.right i)))).base).obj
          (⋯.functor.obj U))),
    D.ιInvApp U ≫ D.diagramOverOpenπ U i = (D.U i).presheaf.map (eqToHom eq)
AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.GlueDa.comment: `ιInvApp` is the left inverse of `D.ι i` on `U`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.condition: The theorem asserts that the composition of the first projection from a pullback with one morphism is equal to the composition of the second projection with the other morphism, establishing a condition that must hold for pullbacks in a categorical context.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.comp_b: This theorem asserts that the base mapping of the composition of two morphisms in a presheafed space is equal to the composition of their respective base mappings.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.congr_ar: This theorem states that if two elements in the underlying type of a concrete category are equal, then applying a morphism to both elements yields the same result.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingMultispan.H: The theorem demonstrates that a morphism from the left side of a walking multispan to the right side, evaluated at a point, results in a specific homomorphism derived from the first function applied to that point.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.lift: This definition describes the morphism that connects the cone point of any cone associated with a functor to the limit object of that functor.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.cancel_mono: This theorem indicates a lack of any specified context, results, or definitions, rendering it effectively empty or undefined in its current form.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingMultispan.H: The theorem establishes that a morphism from the left side of a walking multispan to the right side, evaluated at a point, corresponds to a specific homomorphism obtained from applying the second function to that point.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GlueData.vPullbackCone: This definition describes the construction of a pullback cone for two elements in a category based on glue data and their associated morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.isLim: This definition describes a condition under which a pullback cone is deemed a limit cone by requiring a specific construction relating to morphisms of the cone to another cone.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.IsOpen: This definition describes a unique morphism that can be constructed from a given morphism into an open immersion, provided that the image of the original morphism is contained within the image of the open immersion.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.fst: The first projection of a pullback cone provides a morphism from the cone's point to the first object involved in the cospan formed by two given morphisms.
explanatories.TopCat.GlueData.preimage_range: The preimage of the image defined by one morphism under another morphism in the gluing structure corresponds to the image defined by their connecting morphism in the opposite direction.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GlueData.ι_gluedIso_hom: This theorem establishes a relationship involving the image of a morphism within a functor, stating that it corresponds to the morphism of the glued structure as defined by the glue data, under certain preservation conditions of limits and colimits.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.condi: The theorem asserts that in a pullback cone, the composition of the first projection with its associated morphism matches the composition of the second projection with the other morphism in the cospan.
explanatories.Set.image_subset_iff: The image of a set under a function is a subset of another set if and only if the original set is a subset of the preimage of that other set, illustrating a Galois connection between image and preimage.
explanatories.Set.image_univ: The image of the universal set under a function is equal to the range of that function.
explanatories.Set.image_subset_range: The image of any set under a function is a subset of the function's range.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.IsOpen: This theorem shows that the lifting of a morphism in the presence of an open immersion and a morphism with its range contained within the open immersion's range can be composed with the open immersion to yield the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.forget: This definition describes a forgetful functor that maps objects from a concrete category to their underlying types in a specific universe.
explanatories.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafedSpace.forget: This definition describes a functor that allows one to forget the sheaf structure of a sheafed space and regard it simply as a topological space.

algebraic_geometry.PresheafedSpace.glue_.fullDefinition: def vPullbackConeIsLimit (i j : D.J) : IsLimit (𝖣.vPullbackCone i j) :=   PullbackCone.isLimitAux' _ fun s => by     refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩     · refine PresheafedSpace.IsOpenImmersion.lift (D.f i j) s.fst ?_       erw [← D.toTopGlueData.preimage_range j i]       have :         s.fst.base ≫ D.toTopGlueData.ι i =           s.snd.base ≫ D.toTopGlueData.ι j := by         rw [← 𝖣.ι_gluedIso_hom (PresheafedSpace.forget _) _, ←           𝖣.ι_gluedIso_hom (PresheafedSpace.forget _) _]         have := congr_arg PresheafedSpace.Hom.base s.condition         rw [comp_base, comp_base] at this         replace this := reassoc_of% this         exact this _       rw [← Set.image_subset_iff, ← Set.image_univ, ← Set.image_comp, Set.image_univ]       -- Porting note (#11224): change `rw` to `erw`       erw [← coe_comp]       rw [this, coe_comp, ← Set.image_univ, Set.image_comp]       exact Set.image_subset_range _ _     · apply IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac     · rw [← cancel_mono (𝖣.ι j), Category.assoc, ← (𝖣.vPullbackCone i j).condition]       conv_rhs => rw [← s.condition]       erw [IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac_assoc]     · intro m e₁ _; rw [← cancel_mono (D.f i j)]; erw [e₁]; rw [IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac]

AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.restri.fullDefinition: def restrictStalkIso {U : TopCat} (X : PresheafedSpace.{_, _, v} C) {f : U ⟶ (X : TopCat.{v})}     (h : OpenEmbedding f) (x : U) : (X.restrict h).stalk x ≅ X.stalk (f x) :=   haveI := initial_of_adjunction (h.isOpenMap.adjunctionNhds x)   Final.colimitIso (h.isOpenMap.functorNhds x).op ((OpenNhds.inclusion (f x)).op ⋙ X.presheaf)   -- As a left adjoint, the functor `h.is_open_map.functor_nhds x` is initial.   -- Typeclass resolution knows that the opposite of an initial functor is final. AlgebraicGeometry.PresheafedSpace.stalkM.comment:
If `α = β` and `x = x'`, we would like to say that `stalk_map α x = stalk_map β x'`.
Unfortunately, this equality is not well-formed, as their types are not _definitionally_ the same.
To get a proper congruence lemma, we therefore have to introduce these `eqToHom` arrows on
either side of the equality.
